# Ondin — Architecture

> Ondin is a native, open-source 2D design tool (Figma-class scope, minimal v1) for Windows and Linux,
> written in Rust. Its document model is API-first: the same operation path that serves the UI serves
> AI agents over MCP. Foundations-first — the seams (identity, mutation path, renderer boundary,
> serialization) matter more than feature count, because features are cheap to add and seams are
> expensive to change.
>
> Items under **INVARIANTS** are non-negotiable. If a requested change would violate one, stop and
> surface the conflict instead of working around it.
>
> **This document describes the code as it is.** Where the implementation took a different route
> than originally designed, the section says so and §15 lists the deviation with its reason. A
> design doc that quietly drifts from the code is worse than no design doc — it is the thing
> everyone trusts and nobody can rely on. Keep it honest as you go.

---

## 1. Scope

### v1 — in scope

- Multiple artboards on an infinite canvas.
- Node tree: Root → Artboard → (Artboard | Group | Rect | Ellipse | Line | Path | Text)\*, arbitrarily
  nested groups and frames.
- Layers panel (tree view, reorder, rename, visibility, lock).
- Shapes: rectangle (corner radius), ellipse, line, freeform vector path.
- **Text**: plain-text nodes with a single uniform style (font family/size/weight/style, line height,
  alignment, fixed-box or auto-size). Editable in-canvas. Rich text (mixed runs) is deferred, but the
  node model must not preclude it (see §5.4).
- **Fonts**: all installed system fonts + the full Google Fonts library (on-demand download with
  local cache) + a bundled fallback. Table stakes for designers (see §5.4a).
- Paint: solid + linear/radial gradient fills; strokes with width, join, cap, dash, mitre limit and
  alignment (inside / centre / outside — §6.3 for how, since no backend has it natively), and a
  rectangle's stroke on any of its four sides (§15 D68). **Several fills and
  several strokes per layer**, painted and exported in list order (§5.3, §15 D56).
- **Masks**: any layer that has an outline can be one, clipping the run of siblings drawn above it in
  the same parent — a text node masking with its glyphs and a group with the union of its contents
  included — **by its outline or by its own alpha** (`MaskMode`, §15 D288; luminance is deferred on a
  dependency and is recorded there, not open work) (§5.3, §6.2, §7, §9.4, §15 D282). Asked for on 2026-08-21, which reverses the verdict on
  D191's mask bullet; the reasoning that kept them out until then is untouched and still recorded there.
- **Effects**: a repeatable, ordered stack per layer — **drop shadow, inner shadow, layer blur and
  colour filters** — meaningful on containers as well as on shapes, authored in the inspector's
  Effects card, drawn by the CPU renderer and written by the SVG writer (§5.3a, §6.4, §7, §9.4,
  §15 D333, D337). Asked for on 2026-08-24, which reverses the *Deferred* line below; what stays
  deferred is stated there. Drawn on **all three surfaces** — the canvas, the raster export and the
  SVG file (§15 D339) — from one specification (`ondin_render::effects`). What is not built is a
  drag-reorder of the rows, which is open work in `roadmap.md`.
- Transform: translate/rotate/skew per node (local), about a movable per-node origin (§5.3); resize
  edits geometry, not scale (see §5.6).
- Selection, move, resize, z-order. Copy/paste/duplicate (via `InsertSubtree`, §5.7).
- **Bulk property edits over a selection**: transform, opacity, corner radius and paint set on
  several layers at once, plus recolouring by colour rather than by layer (§9.4, §15 D53).
- Pan/zoom viewport; R-tree culling for many artboards.
- Rulers and **ruler guides**: two ticked bars along the canvas, and the lines dragged out of them,
  each either global or scoped to one frame. The guides are document state, saved with the file
  (§5.5, §9.4).
- **Present mode**: one switch that hides every piece of chrome and leaves the artwork alone, with
  Escape as the way back (§9.4).
- Undo/redo (unlimited, transactional, gesture-granular).
- Save/load native document format (versioned, deterministic bytes).
- Export: SVG (semantic), PNG (via CPU renderer — no GPU required), JSON snapshot (AI handoff).
- MCP server: read/query/export first, then write operations against the live document.
- Headless mode: `ondin serve <file>` — MCP server over a document with no window (see §8.4).

### Deferred (design for, do not build)

- ~~Text-on-path.~~ **Built 2026-09-01 — §15 D405**, and this bullet is now empty of everything it
  ever named. (**Rich text, the OpenType feature UI and per-paragraph attributes are built** —
  §5.4, §9.2. **Text-on-path** was the last of them: a `NodeKind::Text::on_path` rail, with the
  layout bent onto it as a pass over the finished flat one; the "not short of a dependency either"
  above turned out to be right about `kurbo` and wrong about the price, since `text::Glyph` carried
  no rotation and had to gain one. **Hyphenation left it on 2026-09-01 and is now a decided non-goal
  for v1** (§15 D399, `roadmap.md` §0) — declined on price, not blocked: the dictionary crate exists
  and parley already breaks at `U+00AD`, and what was refused is the offset map §15 D80 specifies
  plus a second layout pass. The other two this sentence named are built: lists, with nesting and
  markers (§15 D169, D172), and decoration skip-ink (§15 D356).)
- Blend modes beyond normal, and the two effects that were designed alongside the four above and
  deliberately not built: **background blur** (only meaningful when the export contains the backdrop,
  and inexpressible in SVG at all) and **noise** (three generators that would have to agree to the
  pixel, and probably a *fill* rather than an effect). §15 D333 has the reasoning for each, so none of
  the three is re-argued; `shortcuts.md` §2 still reserves `Shift+3`…`Shift+9` behind the blend modes.
  ~~Filters, blur, shadows~~ — built 2026-08-24, §5.3a.
- Components/instances/variants; auto-layout/constraints.
- Real-time multiplayer — **a real future goal, not a fantasy**. The operation and identity model is
  designed now so it is not precluded (§5.2, §12); the sync layer itself is not.
- **Command Mode** — the keyboard-driven modal workflow (embedded CLI, leap labels, structural
  navigation) that is Ondin's end-game identity. Designed in §13, and its scripting language in
  `vm.md`; v1 only reserves its seams.
- Plugins; prototyping/animation.
- The rest of the image feature. (**Image fills and raster import are built** — the table, the brush,
  the decode cache, placing from the file dialog, drag-and-drop and paste, framing, the inspector row
  that reaches it, **image editing** — the crop gesture, the mode strip and a card of orientation,
  tile scale and *reset crop*, with *original size* on the context menu beside it (§15 D305) — the
  seven per-pixel adjustments, export in all three writers, the
  missing-image placeholder with
  *Replace…* and the layers-row mark, and the layer-row and paint-row thumbnails: §5.5a, §7.1, §9.2,
  §9.4, §15 D176–D191. What is left of this bullet is linked-image loading (§5.5a); what is
  deliberately *not* coming is D191, `images.md` having been folded into this document and deleted —
  minus that entry's **mask** bullet, which the user reversed on 2026-08-21 and which is now in scope
  above.)
- macOS, web, mobile (wgpu keeps macOS cheap later; do not target now).

### Non-goals

Not a general illustration app, not pixel painting, not CAD.

## 2. Stack

Pin all versions in the root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]` at M0; pin pre-1.0 rendering
crates exactly (`=x.y.z`). Known-current as of 2026-07 (verify at scaffold time):

| Concern | Crate | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Toolchain | Rust edition 2024, stable | pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` |
| Windowing | `winit` | `ApplicationHandler` API |
| GPU | `wgpu` | |
| Interactive renderer | `vello` (~0.9) | GPU compute; classic Vello remains Linebender's baseline |
| Export/CI renderer | `vello_cpu` (sparse strips, `=0.2.0` since 2026-09-03) | CPU-only, deterministic; drives PNG export without a GPU. A **PNG** golden would run on it — the SVG and JSON ones do not, and are the two that exist (§11). ⚠️ A raster is **not** stable across versions of this crate: the `=0.0.9` → `=0.2.0` bump moved one mitered outside stroke and nothing else (§15 D414) |
| Geometry | `kurbo` | `BezPath`, `Affine`, `Rect`, `Point`, `Size` |
| Paint | `peniko` | `Brush`, `Color`, `Gradient`; reuse the `color` crate types it re-exports |
| Text layout & editing | `parley` 0.11 (bundles `fontique`) | CPU-only. Layout, shaping, and the `Cursor`/`Selection` cursor model behind `core::text::TextEdit`. `system` feature OFF — core never scans OS fonts |
| Spatial index | `rstar` | R-tree |
| Maps | `rustc-hash` | `FxHashMap` |
| Serialization | `serde` + `serde_json` | native format = versioned JSON (§5.11); binary later behind same API |
| Errors | `thiserror` | |
| UI chrome | `egui` + `egui-wgpu` + `egui-winit` | see §9.1 for the decision record |
| Font acquisition (app only) | `fontdb`, `ureq`, `dirs`, `woff2-patched` | §5.4a. System enumeration, catalog/face downloads, cache dirs, and woff2→sfnt for variable web fonts. None of them may appear in `ondin-core` |

**Renderer-crate churn note.** Vello classic and the sparse-strips renderers (`vello_cpu`,
`vello_hybrid`) are separate codebases that may diverge in rendering details. That is acceptable
because each has a fixed role: GPU Vello renders the interactive canvas; `vello_cpu` renders every
PNG (export, CI, headless) so exported output is deterministic — across machines of one architecture
**and one pinned `vello_cpu`**, because the export path pins the SIMD level (`cpu.rs`'s
`export_settings`) and spells out every rasterizer setting rather than defaulting them (`cpu.rs`'s
`raster_settings`, §15 D414); a stroked path is the one primitive that moves when the level is merely
detected (§15 D304), and it is also the one primitive that moved at the `=0.0.9` → `=0.2.0` bump.
Both live behind
`trait Renderer` (§6). Linebender also publishes renderer-abstraction layers (`imaging`,
AnyRender); we do not depend on them — our own trait is the abstraction — but re-evaluate if
maintaining two backends gets costly.

## 3. Workspace layout & dependency rules

```
ondin/
├─ Cargo.toml                # [workspace], shared pinned deps
├─ rust-toolchain.toml
├─ crates/
│  ├─ ondin-core/            # headless engine: model, ops, history, resolve, text layout, io
│  ├─ ondin-render/          # Renderer trait + Vello GPU impl + vello_cpu impl
│  ├─ ondin-export/          # SVG, PNG, JPEG, JSON snapshot; the export plan and the zip
│  ├─ ondin-mcp/             # MCP server: socket listener + tool dispatch + stdio proxy
│  └─ ondin-app/             # `ondin` binary: GUI shell, tools, panels, `serve`/`export` subcommands
```

**Dependency graph (acyclic):**

```
ondin-core   ← (no internal deps)
ondin-render ← ondin-core
ondin-export ← ondin-core, ondin-render        # SVG needs core plus `ondin_render::effects` for the
                                               # filter maths; PNG/JPEG use the CPU renderer as well,
                                               # plus `image` (the JPEG encoder, already compiled here
                                               # by ondin-render) and `zip` (§7, §15 D274)
ondin-mcp    ← ondin-core                      # ondin-export was declared and used by nothing, and
                                               # was the whole reason the rule below was false (D427)
ondin-app    ← ondin-core, ondin-render, ondin-export, ondin-mcp
```

⚠️ **The SVG line said *"SVG needs core only"* and had been false for as long as effects existed**
(§15 D702). `ondin-export/src/svg.rs` calls `ondin_render::effects` three times — `filter_matrix`
once from the `<filter>` emitter, `any_ink` twice — and that is the **right** arrangement, since §6.4
exists so there is one implementation of the effect arithmetic and a writer computing its own colour
matrix would be a third. What the sentence cost is the reader it is written for: this comment is what
somebody cites to budget an SVG-only path — a `--svg` build, a wasm target, an MCP `export_svg`
handler — for `ondin-core` alone, and such a build gets `ondin-render`, `vello`, `vello_cpu` and
`wgpu`. ⚠️ **Moving the two helpers into `ondin-core` would make the original sentence true and is a
decision rather than a tidy-up**: both are pure over `ondin_core::effect` types and need no
dependency this section forbids, so §3 permits it — but §6.4's reason for `effects.rs` living in
`ondin-render` is that *these functions are the specification the GPU shaders are written against*,
and splitting them puts a shader's colour-matrix order two crates away from the shader.
🚨 **Ruled on and declined** (§15 **D783**, 2026-09-15): the comment above is corrected rather than
made true, because **this section permitting a move is not this document authorising one** — §6.4 is
where the objection lives, and a reader who weighs the question against §3 alone finds only the
permission.

**Allowed-dependency rules (CI-enforced check on `ondin-core/Cargo.toml`):**

- `ondin-core` MUST NOT depend on `vello*`, `wgpu`, `winit`, `egui`, or any GPU/windowing/UI crate.
  Permitted: `kurbo`, `peniko`, `parley` (which brings `fontique`), `rstar`, `serde`, `serde_json`,
  `rustc-hash`, `thiserror`, `base64` (the image table's embedded bytes, §5.5a — zero dependencies of
  its own, and already in the workspace lock through `ureq`), `roxmltree` (the XML half of SVG import,
  §15 D394), `skrifa` and `read-fonts` (the font tables `text.rs` reads directly — OpenType
  feature and name records, metrics and glyph outlines), and `flo_curves` (the boolean solver,
  §15 D91). (`parley` is CPU-only text layout — headless-safe, and core needs it
  for text bounds, hit-testing, and the editing cursor model.) Core must build and pass all tests
  with no graphics context. ⚠️ **This list is load-bearing beyond tidiness, and it omitted the last
  four until 2026-09-06** (§15 D427): the enforcement below is a *denylist* of prefixes, and inverting
  it into the allowlist it should be is blocked on this enumeration being right, since baking a wrong
  allowlist in is worse than the denylist it replaces. **Read against `ondin-core/Cargo.toml` entry by
  entry on 2026-09-07 and exact in both directions** — thirteen names here, the same thirteen declared
  there, nothing extra on either side. That is the check the inversion needs, and it is *set equality*
  rather than "everything declared is listed": a name here that the manifest has dropped would bake a
  permission for a crate nobody depends on, which is harmless today and is how an allowlist stops
  meaning anything.
- Only `ondin-render` may depend on `vello` and `vello_cpu`; `wgpu` is shared with `ondin-app`
  because eframe owns the device and vello and `egui-wgpu` must composite onto one. ⚠️ **This read
  *"`vello`, `vello_cpu`, `wgpu`"* until 2026-09-15 and the wgpu third was *unsatisfiable*** (§15
  D774): `VelloGpuRenderer::new` takes `&Device` and `render` takes `&Device`, `&Queue` and
  `&TextureView`, so nothing can call the GPU backend without naming wgpu types, and eframe puts
  wgpu in the app's tree whatever any manifest says. **The vello half is the half that was true and
  it is tested now** — by a *manifest* scan rather than by the tree walk below, since `ondin-app` and
  `ondin-export` both reach vello through `ondin-render` by construction.
- Only `ondin-app` may depend on `egui`/`winit`.
- `ondin-mcp` contains no rendering or UI dependency. **True and enforced since 2026-09-06** (§15
  D427) — the sentence had been false, `ondin-mcp` declaring `ondin-export` and so reaching vello,
  wgpu and naga through it, on a manifest line no line of that crate's source used.
- **Enforced by `ondin-core/tests/deps_forbidden.rs`, which inspects the *transitive* `cargo tree`
  rather than the manifest** — and reads it `--workspace` rather than `-p`, because with
  `resolver = "3"` those are two different resolutions of the same closure and every gate that
  *compiles* core resolves workspace-wide (§15 D427). ⚠️ **It enforced exactly *one* of the four
  rules above until 2026-09-15, and two of the other three were already false with every gate green**
  (§15 D775). It is a table now — `RULES`, one row per rule a dependency tree can express:
  `ondin-core` and `ondin-mcp` against the headless list, `ondin-render` and `ondin-export` against a
  **second, UI-only list**, which is a separate list rather than a filter because `glutin_wgl_sys`
  arrives legitimately under `wgpu-hal` in both of them. The tree is walked once per row, so a
  forbidden crate elsewhere in the workspace forest is correctly ignored — and once per row rather
  than once with a stack, because `ondin-core` sits *inside* `ondin-render`'s subtree while the two
  rows forbid different things.
- **The vello rule is a second test in the same file**, `only_ondin_render_declares_vello`, reading
  the manifests. It is about what a crate may **declare**, not about what a tree may contain, and
  there is no subtree anywhere in which vello's absence could be asserted — which is why it went
  untested while the others did (§15 D775). **Neither test can express the other's rule.**

## 4. INVARIANTS

1. **Core is headless.** `ondin-core` has no GPU/windowing/UI dependency and is fully testable
   without a device (§3).
2. **Single mutation path.** The only way to change a `Document` is `Document::apply(Transaction)`.
   Node fields are private; no public `&mut` access. UI, MCP, importers, and paste all go through
   operations.
   ⚠️ **The `meta` block is the one carve-out and it is deliberate** (§15 D735). `Document::set_meta`
   is a `pub fn(&mut self)` that replaces the block whole, outside `apply` and outside undo, and six
   production call sites use it. §5.11a carries the argument in full — *"a rename is a library action
   taken from the dashboard, often while the document is not open; routing it through `apply` would
   put an entry in the wrong document's history and make `Ctrl+Z` in the editor undo what the file
   browser did"* — and it reports no `DirtySet`, nothing about the drawing having changed. **The
   sentence above stays true of what it is about**: no node, no edge and no geometry is reachable
   this way, and the block is precisely the part of a `Document` that is *not* the drawing.
3. **Identity is stable, never reused, and caller-minted.** `NodeId = (actor, seq)` where `actor`
   is a random per-session 64-bit id and `seq` a session-local monotonic counter. Ids are minted by
   the *caller* (via `IdSource`) and carried **inside** operations — `apply` never allocates ids.
   Deleting a node never invalidates other ids; undo of a delete restores the identical ids. This
   makes op replay deterministic, which is the property future multiplayer needs (§12).
4. **Document = truth; everything else derived.** `Document` is pure and serializable. `Resolved`
   (world transforms, bounds, R-tree, text layouts) and renderer scenes are derived artifacts —
   never serialized, always reconstructible. No render representation ever feeds back into the model.
   ⚠️ **"Reconstructible" is *from the document plus the registered fonts*, not from the document
   alone** (§15 D735). Text layouts are shaped through the **thread-local** parley engine `core::text`
   owns (§5.9), which holds whatever families the app registered on *that* thread — so
   `Resolved::rebuild(&doc)` on a fresh thread shapes every text node against the two bundled Inter
   faces and hands back different bounds, with nothing to report and no error to raise.
   `Resolved::invalidate_text` is the same fact from the other side: registering a family invalidates
   layouts because the font set is an input. **Latent rather than live** — every rebuild in the tree
   today is on the UI thread, and `library/writer.rs` hands its worker an owned `Document` for
   `io::save` and never a `Resolved` — but as written this invariant *licenses* a worker-thread
   rebuild, and the symptom would be text bounds subtly wrong rather than a failure.
   ⚠️ **`ImageEntry::width`/`height` are the one derived value the document deliberately stores**
   (§15 D788). They come from `ondin-render`'s decoder and are serialized, and nothing re-decodes to
   check them — accepted because entries are content-hash-keyed with immutable bytes, and **decisively**
   because an `ImageSource::Linked` picture's bytes are not in the document at all, so the stored size
   is the only record there is. A link exists precisely because the file may be absent; there is
   nothing to derive it from without one. **Not an oversight, and repairing it by re-decoding on load
   is the mistake this clause exists to prevent.**
5. **Uncommitted state never enters the Document.** Interactive gestures (drag, resize, pen preview,
   text-in-progress) live in app-side preview state and reach the renderer as `RenderOverrides`
   (§6.2) — per-node patches projected from the very transaction the gesture will commit. Exactly
   one `Transaction` is committed per completed gesture. History contains only committed
   transactions.
6. **Local transforms only.** Nodes store transforms local to their parent; world transforms live in
   `Resolved` only.
7. **Color space discipline.** The document stores colors as **sRGB with straight (non-premultiplied)
   alpha** — what designers think in and what serializes stably. Whatever representation a renderer
   backend requires, the conversion lives **only** in `ondin-render` (`color.rs`), and a pin-time
   verification test asserts a known sRGB fill produces the expected output pixel through each
   backend. Do not assume what Vello wants — verify against the pinned version.
8. **Operations are total & validated.** Every operation validates inputs and returns
   `Result<_, OpError>`; never panic on bad input (unknown id, cycle-creating reparent, duplicate id
   in `CreateNode`, a **non-finite number** in a geometry, a transform, a **pivot**, an **effect**, a
   guide position or a paint, etc.).
   ⚠️ **Finiteness is this invariant's job and not the loader's** (§15 D421): `serde_json` cannot carry
   a non-finite `f64` at all, so the operation is the last place such a value can be refused *while
   the user still has their work* — past it the document saves and never opens again.
   ⚠️ **The refusal is per *transaction*, which makes it a rule about the callers as much as about the
   ops** (§15 D481): `Document::apply` is atomic, so one node whose arithmetic overflows costs the whole
   gesture — every well-behaved member of a selection included — unless whatever produced the value
   refuses per node first. `tools::scaled_about` is where a resize does that (§9.4).
   ⚠️ ~~**The code honours that for coordinates and not for paint** (§15 D448). `OpError::NonFinite` is
   scoped to a geometry, a transform or a guide position, and `op_set_fills` validates nothing about
   the brush it stores, so a gradient stop offset of `NaN` goes through `apply` untouched and kills
   `load`. It is blocked at the SVG importer instead, which closes that one route and not the
   operation. **The rule is right and the coverage is short of it** — fix by validating paint here.~~
   **Closed the same day, 2026-09-07 (§15 D451)**: `build::brush_is_finite` is asked by `op_set_fills`
   and by `op_set_strokes`, and it weighs everything a brush can carry — a solid's four colour
   channels, a gradient's kind geometry, every stop's offset *and* colour, the gradient's own transform
   and an image brush's sampler alpha — because the question is what `serde_json` will refuse to write
   rather than what looks like a coordinate. A stroke's `width` and every `dashes` entry go with it.
   **The image arm reached one level further the same day (§15 D452)**: `build::image_ref_is_finite`
   weighs the `ImageRef` hanging off the brush — its crop rectangle, its tile scale and its seven
   adjustment sliders — which are this crate's numbers rather than peniko's, and which a check written
   by reading `peniko::Brush` stops short of.
   ⚠️ **The pivot was inside this rule and outside the code, which is the harder direction to see**
   (§15 D639). `op_set_pivot` validated nothing, so a `Normalized(NaN, 0)` reached the model, saved as
   `null` and made the file unopenable — the same ending as a non-finite transform, reached by a value
   that *looks* exactly like the ones already guarded. `Pivot::is_finite` is the predicate and it lives
   on the enum rather than at either call site, because `Normalized` holds a `Vec2` and `Local` a
   `Point`: a guard written against one compiles happily while missing the other. Two doors ask it,
   `SetPivot` and `op_insert_subtree`'s field loop. **Nothing in this project reads a claim like *"at
   every door that writes one"***, which is the sentence the enforcement test carries and which this
   is the second value to falsify.
   ⚠️ ~~**`OpError::NonFinite`'s own doc and its `Display` string still say *coordinate***, so the rule is
   now wider than the name it is refused under — the same drift that made D451 rename the test. *Fix
   the comment.*~~ **Done 2026-09-07**: both say *number* and both name paint.
   ⚠️ **Effects are the third family, after coordinates and paint** (§15 D641). `op_set_effects`
   checked the node's kind and then stored the list whole, so every number an effect carries reached
   the file by the same route paint did before D451. `build::effect_is_finite` weighs a shadow's offset, blur, spread **and
   colour**, a layer blur's radius and the four filter factors — the colour arm for `brush_is_finite`'s
   reason, that the question is what `serde_json` will refuse to write rather than what looks like a
   distance — and two doors ask it, `SetEffects` and `op_insert_subtree`'s field loop. 🚨 **This family
   is the only one of the three whose value does damage *before* the file is saved.** An infinite blur
   radius reaches `effect::escaped` through `effect::stack_escape`, and there `inf − inf` is `NaN` and
   `f64::min` resolves `NaN.min(0.0)` to the non-`NaN` operand — so the escape is swallowed, the ink
   box comes back as the bare geometry, and the cull, the export plan and both buffer boxes believe an
   unbounded blur reaches nowhere (§5.9). **Answering an infinite box there instead is the failure
   D495 removed**, not the fix; refusing at the operation is what makes the derived function's input
   finite.
   ⚠️ **A number that is finite is not thereby a *usable* one, and `exports` was the field where
   nothing said so** (§15 D492). `op_set_exports` was a `mem::replace` with no bound of any kind, so a
   scale of `Width(0)` or `Times(-2.0)` reached the document and `ondin export --all` wrote a
   `Button@0w.png` of 1 × 1 pixels, exit 0 and nothing clamped. Both other doors onto the same value —
   `ExportScale::from_label`, which the panel's own field goes through, and `main.rs`'s CLI parse —
   already refused exactly that set and said why; the model was the only one that did not.
   `document::export_spec_is_usable` is the predicate now, asked by the operation. Its mirror on the
   loader is a **drop** rather than a refusal (§5.11), because the two doors are answering different
   questions.
   ⚠️ **A third field, and this one was refused at the *resolution* rather than at the operation**
   (§15 D538). `ImageAdjust::pipeline` asked only `is_finite()`, so `"exposure": 1000.0` — finite,
   and therefore already past `image_ref_is_finite` above — made every coefficient of the colour
   matrix `NaN` and painted the photograph solid black in both pixel backends while the SVG writer
   emitted markup no viewer accepts. It asks `-1.0..=1.0` now, which is the range `Adjustment::set`
   has always clamped the panel to. **Three instances is enough to state the shape**: a finiteness
   guard answers what `serde_json` will write, not what the arithmetic downstream can survive, and
   the second question has to be asked wherever the value is *used* if the operation cannot phrase
   it.
   ⚠️ **A fourth, and it is answered by a clamp at the doors rather than by a refusal anywhere**
   (§15 D692). A gradient stop's alpha is a colour component this guard already weighs — for
   finiteness — and a `stop-opacity="5"` is finite, so it survived import, save and load and put
   **500** into a `0..=100` opacity field, from which one bare click rescaled the whole ramp. The two
   places that answer it are `svg_in::stop_of` and `panels::paint::alpha_of` (§5.5a), not
   `op_set_fills`: a stop alpha out of range is a **file** being out of spec, and the model's standing
   choice there is to read such a file rather than refuse it — the same bargain §5.11's export-spec
   drop makes. *So the shape holds and the remedy does not follow from it*: which of clamp and refusal
   is right depends on whether the value arrives from a gesture or from a document.
   ⚠️ **A fifth, and it is the first answered by a *refusal at the operation*** (§15 D767).
   `GradientBrush::opacity` is a `#[serde(default)]` float the loader does not validate, so any six
   characters in a `.ondin` become it — which is **D713's shape one field later**. A non-finite one
   dies at serde, so what `build::brush_is_finite` has to refuse is the **finite out-of-range** one:
   `-5` subtracts alpha and `1e30` saturates every stop opaque, both silently and both surviving a
   round trip. It asks `valid_opacity`, the same predicate a node's own `opacity` uses, per
   `schema.rs`'s *"one answer rather than two spellings of it"*. **The remedy differs from the fourth
   because the subject does**: a stop alpha is a *file* out of spec and is read and clamped, where this
   is a field the app itself writes through `with_alpha`, so a bad one is a bug rather than a foreign
   document and the operation is the last place to say so.
   ⚠️ **A validated operand does not make a usable *derived* value, which is where this invariant
   stops** (§15 D495). `build::affine_is_finite` accepts `Affine::new([1e308, 0, 0, 1e308, 0, 0])` —
   every coefficient of it *is* finite — and the overflow happens two steps later, in the corner
   multiply `geometry::transform_rect` does, so the layer's bounds came out infinite and unioned all
   the way to the root. That is not a hole in the guard above but the boundary of what a guard on the
   operands can see, and the answer is a second one where the value is derived: `geometry::measurable`
   (§5.9). **A property test for this invariant therefore has to assert on derived bounds and not only
   on accepted operands.**
   ⚠️ **An *inverse* is the second way to manufacture one from operands that all passed** (§15 D713).
   `affine_is_finite` accepts a **singular** matrix — every coefficient of one is finite — and
   `Affine::inverse` divides by the determinant, so anything that maps a point back through it writes
   `NaN` into the model from numbers this invariant has already approved. `GradientBrush::transform`
   is the field where that was live: `#[serde(default)]`, validated by nothing on load, so a `.ondin`
   can carry any six numbers, and one click in the picker's `CX` field then wrote a document that
   never opened again (§9.2). `build::affine_is_invertible` is the predicate a *reader* asks before
   inverting — `affine_is_finite(t) && affine_is_finite(t.inverse())` — threshold-free because the
   question is whether the inverse is representable rather than how near zero is near enough.
   **It is the only spelling of that question in the workspace since 2026-09-15** (§15 D762): D713
   counted four others and left them — `> 1e-12` and `== 0.0` in `svg_in`, `< f64::EPSILON` and
   `!is_finite() || == 0.0` in the SVG writer — and all four call this now. 🚨 **`f64::EPSILON` was
   the least defensible and is the one to remember**: it is a *relative* quantity, the gap between
   1.0 and the next double, where a determinant is in *squared world units* — so it stopped guarding
   at large coordinates, and its refusal point had no relation to what it measured. **A number
   chosen because it is spelled like a small number.**
   ⚠️ **The loader still accepts a singular transform, and that is now decided rather than open**
   (§15 D762): normalising one to the identity would silently rewrite the user's file, and worse than
   D713 supposed — a singular transform paints a *degenerate* gradient where the identity paints the
   ramp across the whole shape, so the rewrite makes an invisible paint **visible**. **Geometry with
   no defensible rewrite is carried as written and guarded at the reader**, which is the fourth thing
   this loader does beside refusing a structural error, repairing a recoverable value and dropping
   decoration — a degenerate text rail is already carried that way and refused at layout by
   `PathWarp::of`. The guard is at the readers and every one of them asks it.
   ⚠️ **One rule of the model is enforced as a post-condition rather than by any operation, and it is
   the only one** (§15 D491): after every op in a transaction has been applied and before the working
   copy is committed, `apply` re-checks **every guide's owner**. `check_guide_owner` was asked by
   `AddGuide` and `SetGuideScope` — the two operations that *name* an owner — and the second way to
   break the same rule is to remove the frame, which `op_delete` never looked for. The check is where
   the document becomes real because the rule is about the document rather than about one operation —
   and it is **after the loop** rather than inside it because a transaction is allowed to pass
   *through* a state with an orphan in it: frame-then-guides ends perfectly valid, and a per-op check
   would refuse it (§5.5, §5.7).
9. **Serialization is versioned and deterministic.** Every saved document carries `schema_version`;
   the loader migrates any older version to current. Saving the same document twice produces
   identical bytes (nodes serialized in sorted-id order, stable field order) — the property the golden
   tests rest on, and what makes documents git-friendly. The determinism is real and tested, and since
   2026-08-22 the SVG and JSON goldens do rest on it (§11); the PNG golden is the one still unbuilt.
10. **MCP is a thin adapter.** Tool handlers only translate to/from `Operation`s and queries; any
    logic they need lives in `ondin-core`.
    ⚠️ **Much of the logic the first handlers will need does not live there yet, and the move is
    scheduled rather than done** (§15 D786, `[A2-L7-01]`). `tools/mod.rs` and `preview.rs` hold
    thousands of lines of headless geometry — `resize_box_to`, `rotate_node`, `pen_outline`,
    `pen_anchors`, `insert_point`, `align_points`, `distribute_points`, `space_points` — in a crate
    that declares only `[[bin]] name = "ondin"` and has no lib target, so **nothing outside that
    binary can link any of it**, and §3's graph puts `ondin-mcp` below `ondin-app`. No site violates
    this invariant today because no handler exists; the first one has to move the pure half or
    duplicate it. **The trigger is that first handler, not M6 in general** — D4 defers `serve` to M6,
    so the window is long — and doing it before is a compiler-enumerated sweep where doing it after
    is reconciling two implementations (D2's shape).
11. **Renderers behind one shared walk.** Both backends implement `trait ScenePainter` and the
    document→scene walk is written exactly once, in `scene.rs`. Adding or swapping a backend means
    writing a `ScenePainter` and must not touch core/export/app logic.
    *Correction:* the original design named a `trait Renderer` with a `RenderTarget` object. Both
    existed as unimplemented stubs for two milestones while `ScenePainter` did the real work; the
    stubs are gone and `ScenePainter` is the documented boundary — deviation D2 in §15.
    ⚠️ **The rule is broken from *below* as easily as from above, and that half has no test behind
    it** (§15 D612). A backend that *substitutes* for something the walk left open is deciding, and
    the walk never sees it: the GPU painter answered `clip: None` with a ±1e7 rectangle drawn in the
    **node's own local space**, so an ancestor `scale(0.001)` turned an unclipped layer into a
    clipped one and a layer present in the export was absent from the canvas. Nothing above the
    seam can catch that, because the CPU backend passes the same `None` straight through. **Where a
    backend must supply a value the walk did not, lift the choice into a free function and test it
    there** (§15 D269's shape).
    ⚠️ **The rule says document→*scene* walk, and the SVG writer is not one** (§15 D781,
    `[A1-L7-07]`). `svg::emit_node` re-decides eleven things `scene::build` also decides — visibility,
    opacity, clip, mask and mask mode, effects, fill rule, paint order, the stroke-alignment clip, the
    missing-image placeholder and image framing — so it is **exposure at this invariant's boundary
    rather than a violation of it**, and the agreement was held by convention plus one golden. It has
    diverged twice on record (§15 D179's frame background, and a `fill="none"` on the same path, §7),
    both times caught by a human reading two files against each other.
    `ondin-export/tests/two_walks.rs` is the differential: **the ink set**, node by node, read on both
    sides through per-node colours so neither walk reports on itself. One of the eleven on purpose —
    the two legitimately differ on culling, geometry spelling and element ordering, and both recorded
    divergences were ink-set bugs. **They agree today**, which the finding could not establish by
    reading.

---

## 5. ondin-core

### 5.1 Module layout

```
ondin-core/src/
├─ lib.rs
├─ id.rs           # NodeId { actor, seq }, IdSource
├─ node.rs         # Node, NodeKind, Paint, Fill, Stroke, TextStyle, Pivot
├─ effect.rs       # Effect, EffectKind, Shadow, Filters — the effect stack and its escape (§5.3a)
├─ guide.rs        # Guide, GuideId, GuideAxis — ruler guides; document state, not nodes (§5.5)
├─ layout.rs       # LayoutGrid, GridAxis, GridAlign, tracks() — a frame's columns and rows;
│                  #   chrome over a node, never in the scene (§5.3b)
├─ document.rs     # Document, private tree ops, apply(), remap_subtree, reserve_existing_ids
├─ op.rs           # Operation, Transaction, OpError, ApplyOutcome, DirtySet
├─ build.rs        # composite + bulk-property builders, world-space projection facade (§5.7a)
├─ naming.rs       # the names the app generates for layers, and their numbering (§5.7b)
├─ history.rs      # History (undo/redo stacks)
├─ resolve.rs      # Resolved: world transforms, bounds, text layout cache, rstar index
├─ query.rs        # hit_test, nodes_in_view, bounds, group_chain, pivot_world
├─ geometry.rs     # local bounds per NodeKind; exact hit-testing (point-in-path, stroke distance);
                  #   pivot_point / pivot_for — the one place a Pivot is resolved and chosen (§5.3)
├─ typography.rs   # the text attribute model (§5.4): Length, TextStyle, ParagraphStyle, BlockStyle,
                  #   one generic Spans<A> over CharAttr/ParaAttr, and the boundary rule
├─ text.rs         # parley shaping/measurement + TextEdit (caret model); bundled fallback font;
                  #   font metadata (fvar axes, named instances, GSUB/GPOS features) via skrifa
└─ io/
   ├─ mod.rs       # save/load entrypoints
   ├─ schema.rs    # versioned on-disk DTO + full tree-integrity verification
   └─ migrate.rs   # migrations old→current
```

### 5.2 Identity

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Ord, PartialOrd, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct NodeId { pub actor: u64, pub seq: u64 }

pub struct IdSource { actor: u64, next_seq: u64 } // one per editing session; actor = random u64
```

- Each editing session (GUI, `serve`, an MCP client acting through either) shares the session's
  `IdSource`. A random 64-bit actor id makes cross-session collisions statistically impossible with
  no coordination — the property multiplayer will need.
- The document does not persist an allocator; validation only requires that a created id not already
  exist. Ids of deleted nodes are never re-minted (monotonic `seq` per actor guarantees it).
- Serialized form: `"a1b2c3:42"` (`actor` hex `:` `seq` decimal) — compact and diff-readable.
  ⚠️ **The *reader* is wider than the writer, and nothing asserted a byte of it until 2026-09-09**
  (§15 D662). `NodeId::from_wire` is what every id in every file the app opens arrives through — every
  `parent`, every `children` entry, and every guide id, `GuideId` sharing the function — and it accepts
  five spellings `to_wire` can never produce: a leading `+` on either half, uppercase hex, leading
  zeroes on either half. **None is a defect**: each alias parses to the same `NodeId`, so
  `into_document`'s duplicate check still catches a file spelling one node two ways and a
  non-canonically spelled cross-reference still resolves. An empty half is refused.
  🚨 **Whether they should be *rejected* is open and is the maintainer's ruling**: the case for it is
  the *diff-readable* half of this bullet — a diff is only readable if one id has one spelling — and
  the cost is narrowing what `io::load` accepts, which is a compatibility decision rather than a
  repair. `from_wire_accepts_the_canonical_form_and_six_aliases_of_it` pins the current answer so that
  tightening it is a visible edit.
- **`GuideId(NodeId)` is a newtype over the same id, minted from the same `IdSource`** (§5.5). One
  counter means a guide id and a node id can never collide and that `reserve_existing_ids` covers
  both in one walk; the wrapper is what stops the two being handed to each other's functions, since
  nothing in the model accepts "an id". It shares `to_wire`/`from_wire`, so a guide is the same
  string on disk.

### 5.3 Node model

```rust
pub struct Node {
    id: NodeId,
    parent: Option<NodeId>,
    children: Vec<NodeId>,     // ordered = z-order (last = topmost within parent)
    kind: NodeKind,
    transform: kurbo::Affine,  // LOCAL to parent; translate/rotate/skew/flip — see §5.6
    name: String,
    visible: bool,
    locked: bool,              // set on a container it locks the contents too — §5.10, §15 D321
    proportions_locked: bool,  // a resize holds the aspect ratio; NOT `locked` — see below
    opacity: f32,              // 0.0..=1.0
    clip: bool,                // clip children to this node's own frame; frames only (see below)
    mask: bool,                // this layer paints nothing and clips the SIBLINGS above it (see below)
    mask_mode: MaskMode,       // HOW it masks; remembered while `mask` is off — §15 D288
    paint: Paint,              // shape/text kinds AND frames; empty for Root/Group — §15 D400
    effects: Vec<Effect>,      // shadows, blur, colour filters — §5.3a. Meaningful on CONTAINERS
                               // too, unlike `paint`; empty until someone adds one, and skipped
                               // by the save format
    pivot: Option<Pivot>,      // transform origin; None = the centre of its own box (see below)
    exports: Vec<ExportSpec>,  // the files this layer produces — §7, §15 D274; empty on every
                               // node until someone adds one, and skipped by the save format
    grids: Vec<LayoutGrid>,    // the columns and rows drawn over this layer — §5.3b, §15 D385;
                               // empty and skipped on `exports`' terms, offered on frames only
}

pub enum NodeKind {
    Root,
    Artboard { size: kurbo::Size },         // its ground is `paint`'s fill list — §15 D400
    Group,
    Rect    { size: kurbo::Size, corner_radii: kurbo::RoundedRectRadii }, // per corner; see below
    Ellipse { size: kurbo::Size },
    Polygon { size: kurbo::Size, sides: u32 },                        // regular, first vertex up
    Star    { size: kurbo::Size, points: u32, inner_ratio: f64 },     // inner ring at ratio × radius
    Line    { end: kurbo::Point },          // start is always the local origin (see below)
    Path    { path: kurbo::BezPath },
    Text    { content: String, style: TextStyle, sizing: TextSizing },
}

pub struct Paint { pub fills: Vec<Fill>, pub strokes: Vec<Stroke> } // any number of each; the list
                                                                   // order is the paint order

pub enum Pivot {
    Normalized(kurbo::Vec2),   // a fraction of the node's own box: (0.5, 0.5) is the centre
    Local(kurbo::Point),       // a point in the node's local space, unscaled by anything
}

pub enum MaskMode { Shape, Alpha }   // outline, or the mask's own alpha per pixel. Shape is the
                                     // default. `label()` / `describe()` / `ALL` for the dropdown.
                                     // Luminance is deferred on a dependency, NOT a design choice
                                     // — §15 D288 has the measurement and the re-check trigger.

pub struct Fill   { pub brush: peniko::Brush, pub visible: bool }
pub struct Stroke {
    pub brush: peniko::Brush,
    pub width: f64,
    pub join: kurbo::Join,
    pub cap: kurbo::Cap,
    pub dashes: Vec<f64>,      // on, off, on… empty is solid; the ONLY dash state stored (below)
    pub dash_offset: f64,
    pub align: StrokeAlign,    // which side of the outline the width is laid on (§6.3)
    pub sides: StrokeSides,    // which of a box's four sides it occupies; Rect only (below)
    pub miter_limit: f64,      // the RATIO kurbo and `stroke-miterlimit` take, not the angle shown
    pub dash_fit: bool,        // scale the pattern so whole periods span the outline (§6.3)
    pub visible: bool,
}

pub enum StrokeSides {
    All,                        // the closed outline — what every stroke was before this existed
    Top, Right, Bottom, Left,
    Custom { top: f64, right: f64, bottom: f64, left: f64 },  // independent; 0 = no stroke there
}
pub enum Side { Top, Right, Bottom, Left }   // one side of a box, plus `Side::ALL`
pub enum DashStyle { Solid, Dotted, Dashed, Custom }  // presentation only: classified, never stored
```

- All geometry is authored in the node's **local** space; `transform` positions it under the parent.
- `Line` stores only `end`: the start point is the local origin by convention, eliminating the
  redundant "move the endpoints vs. move the transform" ambiguity.
- **`Path` holds a `BezPath`, and that is a decision rather than a starting point.** A vector network
  — points shared by more than two segments, independently fillable regions — is a *different* model,
  not a richer one, and every reader of a path takes the `BezPath` as the whole of the geometry: the
  scene walk (§6.2), `core::boolean`, the SVG writer (§7) and the save format (§5.11). Nothing in the
  roadmap needs a network and there is no half-step to one. §15 D114 records it so the codebase does
  not drift into one a feature at a time.
- An `Artboard` hangs off the `Root` or off another `Artboard`; what it may never hang off is a
  `Group`. Enforced in validation (`build::can_parent`, the single statement of the rule), and
  `OpError::ArtboardPlacement` is what a violation reads as. **Frames nest** (§15 D62): a frame is a
  page, and a page inside a page is how a card, a component or a state is expressed. A group is the
  exception because it has no box of its own — a clipping page inside one would be clipped by
  something with no edges — and because §5.7a's `paint_targets` relies on no frame being reachable
  through a group.
- **`Artboard` is the type's name; "frame" is the user's.** Every string a designer reads says frame
  — the tool, the default layer name, the nesting error — while the variant, the serde tag and the
  MCP snapshot's `"artboard"` keep the older word. This document uses both for the same reason;
  §15 D21 states which is which and why the split is kept.
- **A `name` is written when the node is created or copied, and never recomputed after that.** A
  fresh node is numbered among its new siblings ("Rectangle 1", then "Rectangle 2") and a copy
  increments a name that already carries a number; the only other writers are the user and a boolean
  relabelled by a change of operation (§9.4). Two siblings may therefore carry the same name, and
  that is legal — §5.7b has the rules, §15 D127 why uniqueness is deliberately not load-bearing.
- **`Root` may also hold loose shapes**, and this is deliberate: a frame is a glorified group, so a
  layer dragged more than half out of one has to land somewhere, and "no frame" is the honest
  destination (§9.4). The rule used to be that `Root` parented *nothing but* artboards, which made
  that gesture inexpressible rather than making documents tidier. Creation agrees with it now as
  well: a shape drawn outside every frame is created at the root rather than adopted by one it is
  nowhere near (§9.4, §15 D25). **Frames now follow the same rule as shapes** in both directions —
  one drawn inside a frame becomes its child, one dragged into a frame joins it, and one dragged out
  lands at the root (§15 D62).
- **`clip` is node-level, not a field of `NodeKind::Artboard`.** It is a property of the *layer*,
  like `visible`/`locked`/`opacity`, and the one container that honours it today is not obviously
  the last one that will — a clipping group is the same switch. `NodeKind::clips_children()` is
  where "which kinds have a frame to clip to" is spelled, and **both ends of the file ask it**: the
  DTO projection normalizes the flag on the way out and the loader on the way in, so an inert `clip`
  neither reaches a document nor survives one (§15 D663). ⚠️ **The flag *can* be set on a kind that
  ignores it, deliberately** — `op_set_clip` lets it sit where `SetMask` refuses the same node (§15
  D282) — which is why the normalization belongs at the format and why doing it at only one end
  moved a document's bytes on its first open-and-save with no edit made. ⚠️ **And the readers do not
  ask the predicate**: `scene::paint_node`, the SVG writer, both copies of `bounds_cover_subtree` and
  `menu.rs`'s layer state all read `Node::clip` itself and kind-gate with a `match` arm where they
  gate at all — so the flag is load-bearing on any kind the moment it is live, and a sentence here
  saying the walk and the writer read `clips_children()` stood until 2026-09-09. It defaults to
  on for frames (Figma's "clip content"), which is what an artboard-as-page means; turning it off
  also turns off subtree culling against the frame, because the frame no longer bounds its
  contents (§6.1).
- **`mask` is node-level for `clip`'s reason, and is not the same switch.** A node carrying it paints
  nothing; its outline clips the **run of siblings drawn above it** in the same parent, up to the next
  mask or the end of the child list — Figma's rule, and what makes a second mask *begin* a second run
  rather than nest inside the first. `clip` cuts a container's *children* to its own frame; `mask` cuts
  its *siblings* to its own outline, and the two must never be conflated. **`Document::governing_mask`
  is the statement of the run rule** — the nearest *preceding* sibling with the flag, and `None` for a
  node that is itself a mask, so a second mask ends the first's run instead of nesting inside it.
  **It is read two ways and both have to agree**: the hit test asks it *backwards*, node by node, and
  it is the function's one production caller, while `scene::paint_node`, the SVG writer's child loop
  and the two bounds passes in `resolve` carry the same rule *forwards* (`MaskRun`, `mask_box`) because
  they are already iterating the child list — a backwards scan per child of a list you are already
  holding would make the walk worse. So **fix a disagreement by correcting the forward reader, not by
  routing it through the function**. The duplication is guarded rather than merely commented: the two
  spellings are asserted against the *same arrangement of siblings*, backwards by
  `ops::a_mask_governs_up_to_the_next_one_and_is_never_masked_itself` and forwards by
  `render::a_second_mask_ends_the_first_ones_run_instead_of_nesting`, so a change to the rule that
  touches one and not the other fails the other. A third arm belongs to both readings: **nothing masks inside a
  `Boolean`**, whose children are operands rather than artwork, so
  the flag on one of them is inert. That third arm does not fall out of anything: the walk never
  reaches those children and so never notices, while the hit test reaches them through the spatial
  index, and without it a mask pasted into a boolean would make part of that boolean unclickable while
  changing nothing about how it draws. `NodeKind::can_mask()` sits beside `clips_children()` and is
  `!Artboard && (takes_paint() || Group)`: **Root and Artboard are the two exclusions**, the root not
  being a layer and a frame already carrying `clips_children` (§9.4 has why a frame that also masked
  would be two switches reading as a pair). ⚠️ **The frame is excluded in writing, and it used to be
  excluded by `takes_paint`** — the spelling was `takes_paint() || Group` while that predicate
  answered `false` for a frame, so widening it to give frames a fill list would silently have handed
  every frame a mask switch beside its clip, with nothing failing (§15 D400).
  Unlike `clip`, the flag is **refused** on a kind that cannot honour it rather than left inert, since
  the walk has to decide whether the layer paints (§5.7). §15 D282 has the whole feature.
- **`mask_mode` says *how*, and it is a field beside the flag rather than a payload inside it**
  (§15 D288). `MaskMode::Shape` — the default, and what every mask made before the mode existed meant —
  clips by the outline, hard-edged; `MaskMode::Alpha` lets the mask's own alpha decide how much of each
  pixel survives, reading its transparency and **not** its colour. The field is separate from the flag
  because the mode has to survive the flag going off and on: set a mask to Alpha, release it to look
  underneath, put it back, and an `Option<MaskMode>` has nowhere to keep *Alpha* in the meantime, which
  makes the toggle quietly destructive. It follows that the mode is writable on a layer that is not a
  mask at all, and that `SetMaskMode` is its own operation rather than an argument of `SetMask` (§5.7);
  `ops::the_mask_mode_survives_the_mask_being_released` pins both. **Luminance — the third mode every
  other editor has — is absent on a *dependency* rather than a decision**: vello's GPU `push_layer`
  takes no mask and no Porter-Duff compose moves colour into alpha, so it is not expressible in the
  compositor and shipping it CPU-only would make the canvas and the export disagree. §15 D288 has the
  measurement and the re-check trigger.
- **`NodeKind::takes_paint()` is the same shape of predicate for `paint`**, and it sits beside
  `clips_children()` in `node.rs` for the same reason. The two containers with no outline of their own
  draw no fills: `Root` is not a layer and a group has no box. **A frame does**, and has since
  2026-09-01 — its fills are `Node::paint`'s list, exactly like every other painted layer's, and what
  is still a frame's own is only *where* the ink lands: behind its children, with its strokes over them
  and outside its clip (§6.2, §15 D144, D400). `Boolean` is the other kind the
  predicate earns its keep on: it is a container that *is* a shape by the time anything draws it (§9.4).
  The inspector's paint panels and the bulk colour edits in `build.rs` (§5.7a) both ask it, so a kind
  added later cannot end up paintable to one and not to the other — a rule the list was copied out of
  twice before it was enforced (§15 D87, D92).
  🚨 **All six `matches!`-over-`NodeKind` predicates are asserted as a matrix now, and the *rejected*
  set is the half that does the work** (§15 D668). `clips_children`, `can_mask`, `takes_paint`,
  `resolve::is_indexed`, `geometry::stroke_sides_apply` and `query::steps_into` each answer `false`
  for a variant nobody added — which is not a compile error, so all six gates stay green and the
  symptom arrives later and somewhere else. `node::kind_fixture` samples every variant behind an
  exhaustive wildcard-free `tag`, so a twelfth kind breaks the compile *there*, and each predicate is
  asserted as the pair of name lists it divides the enum into: asserting the accepted set alone
  converts nothing, since a new variant leaves it unchanged. **`is_indexed` and `takes_paint` have
  identical membership today**, spelled twice in two modules for two unrelated reasons, and they are
  asserted side by side for that reason. ⚠️ What is still unchecked is that the *fixture* is complete;
  the compile error in `tag` is the only thing that ever says a sample was forgotten.
- **`NodeKind::takes_stroke()` is gone, and it existed for exactly one disagreement** (§15 D400). A
  frame's *stroke* is an ordinary stroke list on an ordinary outline, painted over its contents and
  outside its clip (§15 D144), so while a frame could be stroked and not *filled* the stroke side
  needed a predicate of its own — `takes_paint() || Artboard` — and the fill side needed the narrower
  one, or a frame would have drawn a **second** Fill panel beside the card its background already had
  (§15 D397). There is no disagreement left: `op_set_strokes` and the Stroke panel ask `takes_paint`
  like everything else, and `build::strokeable_targets` went with the predicate.
- **`proportions_locked` is node-level for the same reason, and it is the second flag here that says
  nothing about what a node *is*.** Where `visible`/`locked`/`opacity` describe how a layer draws or
  whether it may be touched at all, this one shapes an edit that is already allowed: a resize holds
  the aspect ratio as though Shift were held (§9.4). *It is not `locked`* — that one refuses the
  edit, this one shapes it, and the two are independent in both directions. The field's doc comment
  and the getter's both say so, because that is the confusion the name invites. Unlike `clip` there
  is **no kind gate**: it defaults to `false` for every kind, and there is no kind for which "keep
  the ratio" would mean the wrong thing rather than nothing, so it is simply inert on the rest.
  `remap_subtree` copies it, so a duplicate or an Alt-dragged copy keeps the lock. Set by
  `Operation::SetProportionsLocked` (§5.7) and saved (§5.11), because it is a constraint the user put
  on the layer and forgetting it on reopen was a bug (§15 D41).
- **`pivot` is the node's transform origin, and `None` is a state rather than a value.** It is the
  point a rotation turns about and a mirror reflects across (§9.4) — and **not** what an Alt-resize
  holds still, which it briefly was and could not be (§15 D60).
  `None` means the centre of the node's own box — which is the fixed point every one of those
  gestures already used, so a document nobody has touched behaves exactly as it did — and it is
  stored as an absence rather than as a stored centre so that "the user has not moved it" is
  something the model can *say*: that is what lets the canvas draw the marker only where it means
  something, and what keeps the field out of every file that never moved one (§5.11).
  `geometry::pivot_point` resolves it against a box, and **nothing composes it into the world
  transform** — the gestures that read it bake it into the transform they produce (§15 D55).
  Because resolving it that way turns the absence into a point and cannot report it back, the two
  doors that can *ask* for the absence go through `geometry::pivot_placed_at` instead: it answers
  `None` for the box's own centre, so the marker dragged back to the middle and the Transform card's
  origin fields typed to 50/50 cannot store different things for the same placement (§15 D247). An axis
  with no extent is centred by itself there — it has one position, which is also its middle — so an
  axis-aligned line's origin clears on the other axis alone.
- **The two `Pivot` variants say: normalized where the box is authored, absolute where it is
  emergent.** A rectangle's extent is a field, so a pivot two thirds along it should stay two thirds
  along it when that field changes — that is what a fraction means and what a designer expects of a
  resize. A group's box is its children's union, a line's is degenerate and a path's comes from its
  points, so there is no authored extent for a fraction to be *of*: editing one child would slide the
  pivot out from under everything else in the group. Auto-sized text lands in the emergent half and
  becomes normalized once it has been dragged to a fixed box. `pivot_for` is the single place the
  choice is made, off the same question `tools::resizable_size` asks — is this extent a field typed,
  or a consequence of what is inside? — so the two halves of the rule cannot drift apart. Set by
  `Operation::SetPivot` (§5.7) and saved (§5.11). **Both variants are refused when either coordinate
  is not finite** — `Pivot::is_finite`, asked by `SetPivot` and by `InsertSubtree`'s field loop
  (invariant 8, §15 D639) — because a `NaN` here saves as `null` and the document never opens again.
- **A node's `fills` and `strokes` are both lists of any length, and the list order is the paint
  order**: every visible fill, then every visible stroke, each in `Vec` order, so the last element of
  each list is the last painted (§6.3). Two stacks rather than one interleaved appearance list, which
  is affordable because `StrokeAlign::Outside` covers the outlined-text case that would otherwise
  need a stroke *under* a fill. The inspector presents each list reversed, so its topmost row is the
  last element and therefore the paint you see on top (§9.4). This is not forward-compat headroom and
  has not been since the panels grew a `+`: §15 D56 records the milestone in which the extra paints
  were editable, saved and counted in the bounds while never being drawn.
- **`effects` is a list of the same shape and the same reason, and it is *not* inside `Paint`.** The
  order is the compositing order and two drop shadows at different distances is an ordinary thing to
  want, so it is a `Vec` rather than one slot per kind (§15 D333). It sits on the node because it is
  meaningful on a **container**: a drop shadow on a group and a blur over a whole frame are the
  commonest uses, and neither has a fill to hang from — which is why `Operation::SetEffects` is gated
  on nothing but `Root` where every other paint op asks `takes_paint()`. §5.3a has the model.
- **`sides` needs four nameable sides, so it is the two boxes: `Rect` and `Artboard`** — an ellipse, a
  polygon, a star, a path and a line have no top edge for the word to mean anything against, and text's
  outline is its glyphs', which have no four edges between them. A frame is in it since frames stroke
  (§15 D144), which is the widening D68 held open. `geometry::stroke_sides_apply` is where that list is
  spelled and
  `geometry::effective_sides(kind, stroke)` is the question every consumer is to ask, so the stored
  value is never silently rewritten and a stroke that cannot be put on one side draws the whole outline
  instead of a stray edge — `stroke_expansion` is the one that does not and cannot, which §15 D68 names
  and gives a fix for. That is the same bargain `stroke_align_applies` makes on an open path: the
  control is gated in the panel (§9.2), not the value clamped on the way in. `Custom`'s four widths
  are independent of the stroke's own `width`, and `0` is how a side is switched off — which is the
  only way to ask for two adjacent sides and not the other two. §15 D68 has the mechanism and what
  the bounds pay for it.
- **`dashes` is the only dash state stored, and the mode is classified from it.** `Stroke::dash_style`
  reads the pattern back into the panel's four cells (Solid / Dotted / Dashed / Custom) from the
  *shape* of the value rather than its size, so it is invariant under width and there is no stored
  mode that can drift from the pattern it names. A dot is a **zero-length** dash — `[0, s]` — which
  is what makes `s` unambiguously the centre-to-centre spacing. The two consequences that need
  numbers the model does not carry are resolved at the render boundary instead of written back here:
  a zero-length dash draws nothing under two of the three caps, and fitting a pattern to an outline
  needs that outline's length (§6.3). `dash_fit` is a *flag* for the same reason — write the fitted
  numbers back into `dashes` and the toggle reads as on while being true only until the shape next
  changes size. §15 D69 has both, and the classifier this replaced.
- **`miter_limit` is the ratio, not the angle.** It is the number kurbo takes and `stroke-miterlimit`
  emits — the length of the spike a corner would throw, in stroke widths — and 4 (SVG's and kurbo's
  own default, 28.955°) is what a file without the field means. The panel works in degrees, because
  "corners sharper than this get bevelled" is the question a designer is asking, and
  `node::miter_ratio_of_degrees` / `miter_degrees_of_ratio` (`ratio = 1/sin(θ/2)`) convert at that
  one edge: converting in the model would cost a conversion on every render *and* every export, and
  would write `3.9998` into files. The panel converts *back* only when the angle actually moved,
  because that round trip is not required to be bit-exact: writing unconditionally put a ratio a few
  ulps off the stored one past `strokes_tx`'s equality guard and into the file and the undo stack every
  time the field lost focus. `MIN_MITER_DEGREES` (1°) floors the angle, since the ratio runs to
  infinity as θ → 0. `join` **is** gated by kind, as `align` and `sides` are
  (`geometry::stroke_join_applies`, §15 D68); `miter_limit` is not, and the mitre angle field is drawn —
  dimmed with the Join row it sits inside — on an ellipse carrying a stored `Miter`.
- A rect's corners are **always four radii**, never a scalar with an optional override. A uniform
  radius is the same number four times, so nothing downstream has to decide which of two fields
  wins. `GeometryPatch` still offers `CornerRadius(f64)` for the common "round all of them" edit —
  it is a convenience over the same field, and its inverse is a `CornerRadii`, because flattening
  four values into one is not undoable any other way. ⚠️ **A flatten is a real edit and has to be
  asked for** (§15 D534): the inspector's single radius field shows `largest(corners)` while the four
  disagree, so that a *drag* starts from the shape's own scale, and it handed that seed to
  `edit_valve` on a bare click — turning `(10, 0, 0, 0)` into `(10, 10, 10, 10)` for a user who typed
  nothing. It writes only where the field differs from its seed now, which gives up typing the shown
  number over a mixed set; the per-corner disclosure beside it is that edit's door.
  The per-corner *disclosure* in the inspector
  is app view state (§9.2), not a document property. Radii over half the shorter side are clamped
  where the outline is built (`geometry::local_path`), not on the way in, so shrinking a shape and
  growing it again does not lose the number the user typed.
- **`Polygon` and `Star` fill their box.** Their vertices are placed on a circle and then stretched
  so the outline's bounding box is exactly `0,0..w,h`. That is what dragging a shape out means —
  and, less obviously, it is what keeps `local_bounds` honest: it reports that box, and the
  selection rect, the snap targets and the resize handles all come from it. A triangle merely
  *inscribed* in the circle spans three quarters of its box's height, so every one of those would
  float off the shape. Both share one builder (`geometry::star_path`), because a polygon is the
  star with no inner ring and two copies would drift on the detail that matters: they start at the
  top, so a triangle points up. `sides`/`points` (3..=64) and `inner_ratio` are clamped where the
  outline is built, for the same reason corner radii are.

### 5.3a Effects (`effect.rs`)

```rust
pub struct Effect { pub kind: EffectKind, pub visible: bool }   // mirrors Fill exactly

pub enum EffectKind {
    DropShadow(Shadow),
    InnerShadow(Shadow),
    LayerBlur { radius: f64 },      // the RADIUS as typed, not the deviation — see below
    Filters(Filters),
}

pub struct Shadow {
    pub offset: kurbo::Vec2,        // in the layer's own space, so it turns with the layer
    pub blur: f64,                  // radius, as above
    pub spread: f64,                // dilate (or erode) the silhouette before blurring
    pub color: peniko::Color,       // straight sRGB; the ALPHA is the opacity — no second field
}

pub struct Filters { pub brightness: f64, pub contrast: f64, pub saturation: f64, pub hue: f64 }
                                    // factors, 1.0 neutral; hue in DEGREES, 0.0 neutral

pub const BLUR_DEVIATION: f64 = 0.5;   // deviation = radius × this
pub const BLUR_CUTOFF: f64 = 3.0;      // deviations worth rasterizing — vello_common's own number
pub fn deviation(radius: f64) -> f64;  // what the three writers take
pub fn reach(radius: f64) -> f64;      // what bounds and culling care about
pub fn stack_escape(effects: &[Effect]) -> Insets;              // per §6.4 stage, then the UNION
pub fn escaped(bounds: Rect, escape: Insets, world: Affine) -> Rect;   // local escape → world box
```

- **Four effects, and the four are not an arbitrary subset**: they are the ones expressible on all
  three of the canvas, the raster export and the SVG writer. Background blur and noise are the two
  that were drawn in the same mockup and deliberately left out — §1 and §15 D333 have why, so neither
  is re-argued as an oversight. Per-effect **blend modes** are absent for a third reason: they are
  their own deferred non-goal with a keyboard block reserved behind them, and reversing that deserves
  its own decision rather than a ride-along (§15 D333).
- **`visible` beside the payload rather than removal-as-hiding**, the decision `Fill` already made
  and for a stronger reason here: a shadow is half a dozen tuned numbers, so an `×` that throws them
  away makes "let me see it without the shadow" destructive. The design drew only the `×`; the eye is
  an addition, as are the shadow **colour** and the inner shadow's **spread** (§15 D333).
- **A shadow's opacity is its colour's alpha and is not a field of its own** — and a second spelling
  of alpha is what ends up disagreeing with itself the first time an eyedropper writes one of the two.
  ⚠️ **The rule this cites is *one door*, not *no field*, and §15 D767 is why the distinction
  matters**: a gradient fill's opacity **is** a field of its own now, because scaling a ramp's stops
  is not invertible through zero. What is preserved is the thing the bullet is actually about —
  `paint::alpha_of` and `with_alpha` remain the single pair that reads and writes a brush's alpha,
  whichever of the three arms it lands in. A shadow's colour is a solid, so nothing here changes; a
  reader reaching for "give this a separate opacity field" still owes the argument that there is only
  one door onto it.
- **A blur stores the radius the designer types, not the gaussian deviation**, and `BLUR_DEVIATION`
  is the one place the two are related. CSS spells `blur(12px)` and means a deviation of 6; SVG's
  `feGaussianBlur` and both vello backends take the deviation. Storing the deviation would make every
  panel field divide on read and multiply on write, and would put a number in the save file that no
  part of the UI ever shows. `a_blurs_reach_is_three_deviations_and_a_deviation_is_half_the_radius`
  pins it on a round number, where a dropped or doubled halving is visible in the digits.
- **`Filters` is factors-with-1.0-neutral and degrees, and deliberately *not* `ImageAdjust`'s
  `-1.0..=1.0` with zero neutral** (§5.5a). Two conventions in one codebase is exactly what drifts,
  so the difference is stated rather than quietly carried: `ImageAdjust` is a photographic control
  surface authored against a picture, while these numbers go straight into `feColorMatrix` and into
  the shader, and D186's lesson was that the writer which cannot invent arithmetic should choose the
  units. `Filters::is_neutral` / `changed` answer "is this row doing anything" and "how many channels
  are off neutral" — the panel needs the count and the writers need the first, since a neutral row
  must emit no primitive at all rather than an identity matrix everything has to composite.
- **`escape` is how far an effect's ink lands *outside* the geometry**, as `Insets` read outward, and
  it is zero for a hidden one — that is §15 D56's bug (a paint counted in the bounds while never
  being drawn) in the one place it would recur. A drop shadow's is not one number: the reach is
  `blur + spread` on the side the offset points at and the same minus the offset on the side it
  leaves. An **inner** shadow's is `ZERO` by definition, however far its blur would carry, since it
  is drawn inside the shape's own alpha; so is a `Filters` row's, being per-pixel.
  🚨 **`escape` says where the ink *lands*, and that is not where the passes have to be *evaluated*** —
  two quantities that are equal for every effect here except one, which is why reading either for the
  other went unnoticed in two backends and the SVG writer at once (§15 D742). An inner shadow is cast
  from everything **outside** the layer, so the silhouette it needs reaches `blur + |spread| + |offset|`
  out however little of it lands there. Both renderers get that for free — outside the buffer reads as
  *no layer*, which the complement at the tint turns into *fully casting* — and the SVG writer does
  not, because outside a filter region every primitive's result is transparent black by definition; it
  pads the region (§7). **`ZERO` is the right answer to `escape`'s question and the wrong answer to
  the other one**, and a future reader repairing this bullet towards the pad would break every bound
  in §5.9.
- **`stack_escape` is a union, and it is taken over what §6.4 *composes* rather than over the raw
  escapes.** Two effects each reaching 10px out reach 10, not 20, and summing inflates every cached
  bound on a layer with two shadows — but that is only true of two things drawn side by side, which
  two shadows are and the rest of the stack is not. ⚠️ **It was the plain union until 2026-09-07**
  (§15 D473): §6.4 runs `Filters` and `LayerBlur` sequentially on the layer and casts every shadow
  from *that*, so two layer blurs convolve at `σ = √(σ₁² + σ₂²)` and a drop shadow's silhouette is the
  already-blurred layer. So the answer is **per stage**: stage 1 is one isotropic reach from the
  convolved deviation of every visible `LayerBlur`, stage 2 is each shadow's own escape grown by stage
  1 on every side, and the union is over those. An `InnerShadow` and a `Filters` row still escape
  nothing, whatever stage 1 does. The composition is done in **deviations** and turned back into a
  reach once — squaring and rooting the reaches instead agrees only while `BLUR_CUTOFF` is a constant.
- **`escaped` maps a *local* escape onto a *world* box by splitting it into an offset and a radius,
  rather than transforming four corners.** A blur's reach is a **disc**: read as a local square, its
  rotated AABB is up to √2 too big, so a rotated blurred layer would cache — and export — a box 41%
  too wide. The offset is a vector the linear part maps directly; the radius becomes the exact
  half-extents of the mapped ellipse, which is the row's euclidean norm and not its absolute row sum.
  The four-corner version is the one anyone writes first and it looks completely reasonable;
  `a_rotated_blur_reaches_its_radius_and_not_its_diagonal` is what says so, answering 14.142 against
  it. It also **never shrinks** a box — a shadow thrown entirely to one side leaves the geometry's own
  edge needing coverage on the other.
- Written by `Operation::SetEffects` (§5.7), cached into `Resolved::ink_bounds` (§5.9), drawn through
  `ScenePainter::push_effect_layer` (§6.2) by the passes in §6.4, exported as one `<filter>` per node
  (§7), and saved as an additive `NodeDto::effects` (§5.11). Authored in the inspector's **Effects
  card** — one row per effect, each with a popover behind it (§9.4, §15 D337) — and, for the same
  reasons every other panel does, through the operation as well.

### 5.3b Layout grids (`layout.rs`, §15 D385)

```rust
pub struct LayoutGrid {
    pub axis: GridAxis,      // Columns divide the width, Rows the height
    pub count: u32,          // 0 draws nothing rather than being refused — `sides`' rule, and
                             // `tracks` clamps the top end at MAX_TRACKS for the other half of it
    pub gutter: f64,         // between one track and the next
    pub margin: f64,         // frame edge to first track; BOTH edges under Stretch, one under
                             // Start/End, not read at all under Center
    pub size: f64,           // a track's width/height; read unless Stretch, which derives it
    pub align: GridAlign,    // Stretch | Start | Center | End
    pub color: peniko::Color,
    pub visible: bool,     // this grid's own eye — document state, saved. The workspace switch
                           // (View ▸ Show layout grid) is a third gate above it and never writes
                           // here — §15 D755
}

pub const MAX_TRACKS: u32 = 10_000;                          // most tracks one grid draws — §15 D488

pub fn tracks(grid: &LayoutGrid, size: Size) -> Vec<Rect>;   // the bands, in the frame's local space
pub fn next_grid_color(existing: &[LayoutGrid]) -> Color;    // the first of GRID_COLORS nobody is using
```

- **Chrome, not ink.** A layout grid is drawn over a frame and is never in the artwork: no scene
  node, nothing in any export writer, nothing in the snapshot. `Operation::SetLayoutGrids` therefore
  answers **false** to `changes_ink` beside the guide operations, for the reason that list already
  gives — *a guide is a line over the artwork rather than part of it* — and `RenderOverrides::absorb`
  treats it as a no-op. ⚠️ **Those two lists are *not* the same eleven, which this bullet asserted
  until 2026-09-09** (§15 D659): `changes_ink`'s eleven are a **subset** of `absorb`'s thirteen
  no-ops, the two extras being `AddImage`/`RemoveImage`, which are absorbed for want of an image table
  to patch rather than for being invisible (§6.2). The test that pins the eleven asserts its own
  length, and `overrides.rs` has the sibling that pins the thirteen.
- **A field on the node, offered on a frame.** `Node::grids` sits beside `exports`: empty on every
  layer until somebody adds one, skipped by the save format, ignored by every walk. That is `clip`'s
  arrangement — a property of the layer, inert on kinds nobody offers it for — and what confines the
  *offer* is that a grid is measured against an **authored** size, which `NodeKind::Artboard` has and
  a group's derived box does not. ⚠️ It is **not** normalized away on load for other kinds, unlike
  `clip` and `mask`: those are booleans that would change behaviour on the wrong kind, and a grid list
  is read by one panel and one overlay that both ask the kind first.
- **Nothing is a mode with a payload.** `GridAlign` decides which numbers are read; every one of them
  is a field beside the mode, so switching to *Stretch* and back finds the track size the user typed.
