thing (§15 D269). The cursor announces the pan with a hand and gives a handle
the stock **resize** cursor, which is the honest one: what a crop handle moves is the layer's own
edge, and the ghost is what says the picture stays behind.

**The way out with the mouse is a *Done* pill in the size badge's slot** (§15 D270). D268 took the
crop tool off the rail and removed the pointer's exit with it — a rail button is a way *out* as well
as a way in — leaving `Enter`, `Escape` and picking another tool, none of which a pointer can reach.
`canvas::crop_exit_pill` puts it back: the same ground, ink, radius, gap and `badge_placement` the
size badge uses, since `color::BADGE` *is* `color::SELECT` and "a light blue pill under the box" is
what that badge already is. The slot is free by construction — `chrome_hidden` is true throughout the
mode and both the badge and the origin fields are drawn inside that guard — so it is still one
readout at a time. It is a `Foreground` `Area` like the origin fields, so egui shields it from the
canvas by itself (§15 D252), and `wheel_input`'s exemption names its layer too, or scrolling would
die over it (§15 D254). ***Done* rather than *Exit* or *Save*:** every drag commits on release
(§9.3), so there is nothing unsaved to save and no work to discard.

**None of that chrome had ever drawn**, and it is worth stating here rather than only in the ledger,
because the shape of the fault is a design one: `draw_crop_box` was called from inside `draw_points`,
which returns unless the *node* tool is editing a path, so it could only run in a state with no crop
in it. The crop tool therefore shipped with no box at all while `chrome_hidden` faithfully took the
selection's away. Fixed by hoisting the call to `draw_canvas` beside `draw_points` itself; the shapes
are lifted into a free `canvas::crop_chrome` so that a test can look at them (§15 D269). **Where a
`&mut self` method is *called from* is still not testable in this crate** — that half is the user's eye,
and it is the half that stayed wrong, and it is the one thing `OndinApp::headless` does *not* change
(§15 D303).

**A picture also arrives by being dropped on the window or pasted** (§15 D183). `take_dropped_images` runs
every frame from `update` **unless `OndinApp::modal_is_up`** (§15 D759 — the drop is the pointer half of
D464's guard, and `raw.dropped_files` is filled from winit before any widget runs, so no backdrop stops
it), whatever the tool is, and reads `raw.dropped_files` — a drag out of a browser
arrives as bytes and a file-manager drop as a path, and both end at the same loader the file dialog uses.
The drop lands at the pointer, cascaded 24 units per file so several do not stack into one, and at the
viewport centre when there is no pointer over the canvas. **However many files it carries, a drop is
one transaction and one undo step** (§15 D522): it called `create_image_at` per file until
2026-09-07, which commits its own, so three pictures were three steps and one `Ctrl+Z` left two of
them behind with only the last selected. The placements are built through `canvas::image_tx` against
a document **advanced as each one is added** — the index, the free layer name and "is this blob
already embedded" are all read off the tree — while *where* each picture goes is read from the live
document either way, a picture being no container and `draw_target` needing the camera as well. Every
picture the drop made is selected, not the last. **On Windows nothing the OS sends during a file
drag carries a position** (§15 D184), so the pointer there is the *desktop cursor*, read through
`GetCursorPos` and mapped into egui's screen space against `ViewportInfo::inner_rect` — one Win32 call,
behind `canvas::os_cursor_desktop_px`, asked before the event stream rather than after it because during a
file drag egui's own pointer is absent or one frame stale (§15 D241). Dropping a *single* picture **onto**
the **selected** shape replaces that shape's image fill and keeps its crop, mode, tile scale and
orientation; the **chord's** paste addresses the selection with no point at all, and the context menu's
*Paste here* has a point and is therefore aimed like the drop — a selected shape under the press, or a new
layer at it (§15 D224). Anything else makes a layer, fitted
exactly as a click-placed one is. While files are over the window, `canvas::draw_drop_indicator` says which of the two a release
would do — an outline round the frame that will take the picture (`target_artboard`, with a border inside
the canvas edge as the fallback), a pill naming the outcome, and the hover outline on the shape that
would be replaced (§15 D184). SVG is refused with a message rather than rasterized. The paste is the odd half: `Ctrl+V` over a picture-only clipboard produces no egui event
at all, so `input::normal_mode` reads the key *release* as well as `Event::Paste` and `Action::Paste` tries
the picture before falling through to the in-app layer paste.

Point editing itself is complete — adding a point on a
segment, bending a segment directly, a marquee over points, keyboard anchor navigation and numeric handle
fields were all listed here as missing long after D120–D123 built them.

### 9.5 The library (§15 D362–D366)

**The app has two screens and the dashboard is one of them, not a panel over the other.**
`OndinApp::ui` calls `dashboard_ui` and **returns** — before the font poll, before `input::resolve` — so
while the library is up there is no tool, no selection to nudge and no canvas to autopan. The boundary
is at the top of the frame on purpose: that makes it a property of the frame rather than a rule every
panel has to keep. **Three things are given up by returning this
early and each is deliberate**: the font poll, which the dashboard needs for nothing; `disk_results`,
whose pill the editor's panels draw; and the two ticks, one of which `go_to_dashboard` compensates by
hand and says so.

⚠️ **The close interception used to be a fourth and was not deliberate** (§15 D526).
`handle_close_request` — *"intercept the window close so unsaved work is never lost silently"*, a claim
about the **window** — and `close_confirmation` with it sat below this return, so on the library screen
the ✕ was never intercepted whatever the session held. Both are above it now, beside `recovery_modal`,
which has been there since D377 for the same reason. The argument for the boundary is *no tool, no
selection, no canvas*, which is an argument about the editor's own machinery; it never was one about
the window, and the ordering is unchanged for everything except the close.

⚠️ **That early return is also what left this screen with no voice, and it has a status line now**
(`app::status_label`, §15 D426). `EditorSession::status` is one slot, and its only reader sat below the
return — so the **22** messages `panels::dashboard` writes were painted nowhere: a *Delete project*
that could not read `projects.json` closed its confirmation, left the project in the sidebar and said
nothing. The message was not even cleared; it surfaced later, out of context, in the editor's top bar
the next time a document was opened. 🚨 **The two screens draw it differently on purpose, and only
the *colour* is shared** (§15 D751). The editor's bar draws the sentence (`app::status_label`); the
library draws `app::status_dot`, a fixed 8pt mark in a 28pt hit box with the whole message on hover.
It was one function with a `max_w` until 2026-09-10, and the library passed
`(bar width − SEARCH_W) / 2 − 48` — half the leftover room beside a **painted** search field, which
is a function of the window: 382pt at the default 1200, 22pt at 500, **zero at 436**, and there is no
`with_min_inner_size` on the viewport. So the report faded out exactly where present mode says the
user is working. `app::status_color` is the one statement that stayed shared: *what a failure looks
like* is the thing the two screens must not disagree about, and it is now the only thing on the
library's bar that separates a failure from a report. ⚠️ **A dot cannot be asserted the way the
sentence was** — a tooltip's ink never reaches `.shapes` — so the three tests watching this split
their assertions: the dot and its colour for the surface, `session.status().text` for the wording.
*Asserting the text alone is the bug this whole passage is about.*

**Storage.** One base folder, defaulting to `~/.ondin` and user-settable. Nothing asks where to save,
where to open, or what a file is called on disk:

- `<root>/<slug>.ondin` — a document. `<root>/<project folder>/<slug>.ondin` when its project has a
  folder. The typed name is slugged (`library::naming`), collisions take `-1`, `-2`, and Windows
  device names go through the same path because `nul.ondin` opens the null device.
- `<root>/projects.json` — the project list: id, name, colour, optional folder, and an `archived`
  flag written only when it is true (§15 D379).
- `<root>/.versions/<document id>/<unix seconds>.ondin` — pinned versions, keyed on the id so a
  rename cannot orphan them. ⚠️ **Written and never read back** (§15 D699): `store::pin_version` is
  reached from `save_file`, and `store::versions` — the function that lists the directory — has no
  production caller at all, so this is a history the app accumulates and offers nowhere. It carries an
  `#[allow(dead_code)]` naming the gap rather than a `#[cfg(test)]` hiding it.
- `<root>/.trash/` — deleted documents, kept for a configurable window. **The window runs from a
  stamp written on the way in**, because `fs::rename` preserves the original mtime and there is
  nowhere else to put a deletion time: the metadata block carries no clock (§5.11a) and a sidecar
  index is the thing the trash exists without. So `store::trash` touches the moved file and
  `store::trashed` reads it back — the one place in the library an mtime is written rather than read.
  ⚠️ **The window is swept at launch** (`OndinApp::open_at_launch` → `store::purge_trash`, §15 D550),
  and until 2026-09-08 it was swept by pressing *Save* on the library-settings card and by nothing
  else — that handler's last line was `purge_trash`'s only caller in the workspace. So the Trash
  heading's *"kept for 30 days"* and this bullet's *configurable window* were both claims nothing
  kept, and changing the **autosave interval** in that card was a silent retroactive purge of
  everything past the window. The card still sweeps, which is what makes a window the user has just
  *shrunk* take effect now rather than at the next launch; the launch is what reaches the user who
  never opens the card, and it is a launch rather than a walk into the dashboard because
  `reopen_last` goes straight into a document and may never show the library at all.
  ⚠️ **A read-only document refuses exactly that touch and nothing else** (§15 D432): the rename is
  allowed and so is the eventual delete, so the failing step was the one whose result was being
  discarded, and a document deleted after a year untouched was purged by the very next sweep while the
  screen said it was kept for thirty days. The attribute is now cleared for the length of the stamp and
  the *original* permissions put back, a document being marked read-only in order to be protected and
  the trash being the only undo the library has.
- `<root>/.recovery/<key>.ondin` — a crash snapshot of an open document, keyed on its id or on a
  minted key when it has none. Not a document until somebody says it is (§15 D377). ⚠️ It is the one
  thing here nobody would expect on their other laptop — in-flight work belonging to one machine and
  one run — and it lives in the base folder anyway, so the library stays one directory to back up,
  move or point a sync client at.
- `dirs::cache_dir()/ondin/` — everything derived and local: last-opened times, stars, covers. **Not
  in the base folder, and that is the line**: what a user would expect on their other laptop goes in
  the document (§5.11a); what they would not, goes here (§15 D366).
  ⚠️ **The cover cache is one directory for every library, and `Covers::sweep` keeps only what the
  *current* one claims** (§15 D708). It runs once per entry into the dashboard, over
  `dirs::cache_dir()/ondin/covers`, deleting every PNG whose stem is not `cover::key` — id plus mtime
  — of a document in `library.entries`, which is also what removes the superseded covers of documents
  that are still here. Nothing in the path and nothing in the key namespaces per library, **so
  changing the base folder throws away the old library's covers and switching back re-renders all of
  them** at one document per pass. That is affordable because covers are disposable, and it is stated
  here because it was stated nowhere: a doc comment on `Covers::clear` was claiming the opposite, and
  a rule about the whole cache written on one function is invisible to anyone changing either.

⚠️ **A `Project::folder` is a single path component, and until 2026-09-06 only its doc comment said
so** (`library::project::is_folder_stem`, §15 D420). With `"folder": "../.."` every *New file* into
that project is written outside the library, *Move to project* renames a document out of it
permanently, and `rename_folder` — which `fs::rename`s `root.join(old)` with `old` taken straight off
the file — moves whatever `"../../../Users/<you>/Documents"` names *into* the library under a slug.
Checked with `Path::components` rather than by looking for separators, so a drive prefix, a UNC root
and `.`/`..` in any position are all caught. Enforced in `Projects::read`, the single reader — which
is also the door `relocate::merge_projects` adopts another library's records through, so pointing
*Change base folder* at a received directory is the delivery route and it needs no local attacker. A
bad value is **dropped rather than refusing the file**, the same trade `DocumentMeta::sanitized` makes:
`None` means "this project keeps its files at the root", so the project still appears and nothing is
hidden.

⚠️ **Changing the base folder can *migrate* the library, and the session is re-pointed through the map
that migration returns** (`library::relocate`, §15 D430). `session.path` is absolute, so leaving it
alone left the editor saving into the folder the library had just abandoned — recreating the document
there beside the copy `relocate` had already carried across, under the same `meta.id`: two files, one
identity, with the library listing only one of them and every later edit going to the other.
`prefs.last_document` is re-pointed with it. **A map of `(from, to)` pairs and not a prefix swap**,
because `relocate` renames into a collision, so a caller re-joining the relative path under the new
root can land on a file belonging to a different document; `Moved::documents()` is derived from the
same pairs, so the status line and the map cannot disagree about which files went.

⚠️ **A failure is *named* rather than counted, because the recovery is manual and has to be** (§15
D620). `Moved::failed` is a `Vec<PathBuf>` of **source** paths — a failed move leaves the file where it
was, `move_file` being copy-then-delete with the delete last — written through the single
`Moved::fail(&Path)` spelling so that none of the twelve failure sites can record a loss without saying
what was lost, and `summary()` puts the first of them in the status line. The user has to go and find
what stayed behind: `apply_library_settings` re-points the app at the new root whether the migration
succeeded, partly succeeded or did nothing, and running it again leaves duplicates rather than being
idempotent, so there is no retry and no rollback to offer instead. A number cannot be acted on; a name
says which folder to open and whether what is still there is a document or a sidecar.

⚠️ **"Into a collision" is now the whole of when it renames, and it was a partial truth until
2026-09-07** (§15 D509). Every stem was re-derived from `Entry::display_name()`, which is a silent
rename of every document in the library — and **the sync-conflict mark (§15 D375) exists only in the
filename**, every pattern of it being one `naming::slug` cannot produce, so re-slugging is the one
operation that erases it. `landing-v4 (1).ondin` arrived as `landing-v4-1.ondin`, unmarked and sharing
the original's `meta.id` (a conflict copy carries the original's block), and two entries under one id
collide on `.versions/<id>/`, the star, the *Recent* row, `cover::key` and `recovery::pending`'s
lookup. The name a file already has is kept wherever it is free at the destination;
`naming::unique_stem` is the fallback and is what merging two libraries needs.

⚠️ **A collision means something different in each of the three dot-directories, so the merge has three
policies** (§15 D431). In `.versions` it is the same document at the same instant, so the arrival is
skipped and nothing is lost. In `.trash` it is two unrelated documents that happen to share a name —
`store::trash` uniquifies within one folder and knows nothing about any other — so the arrival is
**renamed**, where skipping stranded a document in a folder the app no longer reads, uncounted, under
a status line reporting success. In `.recovery` it can be neither: a snapshot's stem *is* a document
id, so a renamed one would be offered to the user and then be undiscardable, and the file is left
where it is and **counted as a failure** so the summary says so.

⚠️ **The scan walks two levels and skips dot-directories.** A document sits at the root or inside a
project folder, so that is the whole tree; `.versions`, `.trash` and `.recovery` hold real `.ondin`
files that are *not* library entries, and the leading dot is the only thing distinguishing them.
⚠️ The two rules overlap: `.versions` is three levels deep and excluded by the depth limit as well, so neither can be
changed while assuming the other still covers it.

⚠️ **A scan that could not read the folder is not evidence that the folder is empty (§15 D384).** The
unit that goes missing is never one document — a document cannot live outside the base folder — it is
the whole library: an unplugged drive, a sync folder that has not mounted and a base folder renamed in
Explorer all come back as an empty list, which is also what a fresh install comes back as, since
`~/.ondin` is created by the first write rather than at launch. `Library::root_unavailable` is the two
facts together — the folder could not be listed **and** the per-machine index has something in it,
which is this computer saying it has seen documents here. Three things hang off it. The sweep that
drops per-machine rows for documents the scan did not find (`LocalIndex::retain_known`) runs **only
when the folder was actually read**, or one launch with the library offline takes every star on the
machine. The empty state answers before the nav does, because "nothing starred" and "the trash is
empty" are sentences about a *filter* and are both lies here. And the three doors that create a file
refuse rather than proceeding — ⚠️ **not a nicety, since every write here begins with a
`create_dir_all`**: without the refusal, *New file* succeeds into a brand-new empty folder wearing the
missing library's name, and the sync client that restores the real one then has two libraries to
reconcile. ⚠️ **The index is keyed by document id rather than by folder**, so the second half of that
flag is a fact about the *machine* — which is why Settings creates the folder it is pointed at rather
than opening a library that refuses the write that would have made it.
⚠️ **That creation is the *first* thing the branch does and its failure is the refusal** (§15 D700).
It sat at the foot of the block as a `let _ = create_dir_all(…)` until 2026-09-09, after the migration
had run and after `prefs.base_folder` had been assigned, so a path naming an existing **file** — a
mis-copied path, a `.lnk`, a sync placeholder — was adopted anyway and *persisted*, so `may_write`
went false, `root_unavailable` true, the listing empty, the state survived a relaunch, and the card
said nothing at all. With the migration on, `relocate` had already run against a destination that
cannot be a directory. **Only the base folder is refused**: the card's other settings
were applied above and an early `return` would discard the autosave interval because a path was
mistyped, which is a second surprise. The sentence saying so is asserted on the screen and not on
`session.status().text`, per §15 D605.

**Dates are local, differences are not (§15 D384).** The *Created* column converts through
`clock::local_offset`, which asks Windows for the offset **at that instant** rather than today's —
`GetDynamicTimeZoneInformation` plus `SystemTimeToTzSpecificLocalTimeEx`, the `Ex` because the
year-by-year rules hang off the zone's registry key, so a stamp from last July and one from January
come back an hour apart as they should. The relative labels beside it ("2h ago", "Yesterday") are
differences between two instants and have no timezone in them at all. Off Windows the offset is zero,
i.e. UTC, which is what every date in the app read until 2026-08-28.

⚠️ **A record that could not be read is never written over by the defaults that read produced** (§15
D418). Three files the app reads at startup carry a latch — `Prefs::unreadable`,
`LocalIndex::unreadable` and `Library::projects_unreadable` — set when the file exists and cannot be
parsed, and checked by every write. Without it a single half-synced file costs every star on the
machine at the first click after launch, since the doors are ordinary: every open, every star, every
search. **The latch alone would be worse than the loss it prevents**, because all three states look
exactly like an ordinary empty one from the screen — a library with nothing in it, a *Recent* list
that has forgotten, no projects — and the user's obvious repair for an empty library is to make a new
one *beside* the real one. So `OndinApp::report_unreadable_records` says so once, into the status line
above, naming `base_folder` in particular because it is the one preference whose loss is not cosmetic.
A `fail` and not a modal: all three states are survivable and the app runs. Each record gains a
`load_from`/`save_to` pair against an explicit path, because `load` and `save` read
`dirs::cache_dir()` with no injection point and a probe driving them would read — and overwrite — the
developer's own files (§15 D370).

⚠️ **That pair is available and it is not what the app calls, so the suite still writes to the real
cache directory** (§15 D619). `remember_search` ends in `LocalIndex::save` and `Library::open` begins
in `LocalIndex::load`, both the global spellings, so a test driving anything at the `OndinApp` level
goes through them however carefully its fixture redirects the base folder — which is a *different*
knob. It surfaced as a test finding its own *Recent searches* already populated from the previous
run. The rule above is right and is only half-enforced: **an injection point for the local index is
open work**, and until it exists a probe that reaches this path has to assert persistence through
`save_to`/`load_from` on a temp path and say so.

**Every write is metadata first, path second.** A rename writes the name into the document and *then*
renames the file; a move writes the project id and *then* moves the file. The failure that leaves is a
stale filename with a correct name inside — which the dashboard reads right, and the next rename fixes.
The other order fails into a file whose name and contents disagree with nothing to say which is right.

⚠️ **And the open session is a third copy of that metadata, which has to be patched with it** (§15
D429). Those writes land in the *file*; the session's `Document` is what the next save serializes, so
re-pointing `session.path` alone meant **the next save undid the operation**, writing the old name or
the old project id back into the file the user had just moved. `OndinApp::open_document_follows` is
the one spelling — the guard, the clone and the write-back, with the field as a closure — and it is
called from all four doors that move a library file. The worst of them was *Delete project*'s
**transfer** branch, which followed nothing at all, so the next autosave recreated the document in the
deleted project's folder and the library came to hold two files under one `meta.id` — the key version
history, the cover cache and `recovery::pending` all match on.

**Nothing in the library is undoable.** These are not document edits, so *Delete* moves to `.trash`
rather than removing anything, and that is the only undo the library has. Deleting a *project* is the
exception with no trash at all — it was never anything but a row in `projects.json` — so its dialog
settles the files before the row goes.

🚨 **That ordering was doing nothing until 2026-09-08, which is the sharper half of the rule** (§15
D556). `delete_project` moved the files first and then removed the row **unconditionally**, so a run
that failed halfway removed it anyway — the row gone, the documents still on disk carrying a project
id `Library::project_of` reads as unfiled, and the whole of it silent, the failure count's only
consumer being a status line. The row and the nav reset are both gated on every member having moved
now, so the state a partial failure leaves is the one the ordering was chosen for: the project still
there, holding whatever could not be moved, and *Delete project* pressed again retrying exactly those
members. **The nav reset is the half worth naming** — resetting to *All files* on the failure path
takes the user off the one heading that holds the files they have to deal with, which is the screen
where the retry is one click away.

**A project can be edited, and archived rather than deleted (§15 D379).** *Edit project* sits beside
*Delete project* in the body header and opens the New project card with two rows swapped: *Create
folder* — a decision that belongs to creation — is gone, and an *Archive project* switch is in its
place. The name, the colour and the flag are written to `projects.json`; a **rename takes the
project's folder with it**, which is the one thing that folder was ever for, and the open document
follows the folder exactly as it follows its file through a move — path **and** metadata, per the rule
above, which is the half this sentence promised and did not have until §15 D429. ⚠️ A rename can *fail* on the disk
and succeed in the record, so `library::project::rename_folder` returns the stem the move actually
produced — which may have stepped around a collision — and the caller records that rather than the
one it asked for.
⚠️ **Nothing edited, nothing written** (§15 D719). The card is seeded from the project, so opening it
and pressing *Save changes* — or Enter — used to reach `save_project` with every field equal to what
was stored and run the whole sequence anyway: rewrite `projects.json`, re-read it, and **rescan the
library**, a price `refresh` accepts on the assumption that something moved. The cost that matters is
not the work but the *message*: a write that fails then reports *"Could not write projects.json"*
about a change the user did not make, on a screen that has had a status line to say it on since §15
D426. `EditProject::differs_from` is the mirror of `EditProject::of` and is asked **twice** — once by
`save_project`, which is what covers Enter and a card that went stale while it was open, and once by
the footer, which dims the button. That is `set_archived`'s `if p.archived == archived { return; }`
asked of the whole card. ⚠️ The name is compared **trimmed**, because `save_project` stores
`name.trim()` and a trailing space is therefore not an edit. ⚠️ **The two project cards still
hand-roll their footers** rather than calling `settings::modal_footer` — see the card paragraph
below — so the *rule* is shared now and the control is not.

**Archiving is a flag and nothing else.** It moves no file, touches no document's metadata and does
not remove the project: an archived project still owns its files, still counts them, and still has a
page of its own. What it loses is every *list* a project appears in — the sidebar's *Projects* group,
*Recent*'s project cards, the header's filter and *Move to project* — so it becomes reachable only
from the sidebar's collapsible *Archived projects* group, which appears once there is one to hold and
is **collapsed on every launch** rather than remembered. ⚠️ Two deliberate exceptions, both because
the thing being asked for is not a choice among projects: **search** still matches an archived project
by name, and the *Move to project* sheet still shows the archived project a document is *already* in,
because a destination list that omitted it would draw the sheet as though the document were unfiled.
`Projects::active` is the predicate for every list; `Projects::get` is deliberately unfiltered, since
a document filed in an archived project must still resolve to its name and its colour.

⚠️ **A *destination* is a third question and needed its own name** (`Projects::destination`, §15
D557). *May a new document be filed here* is neither a list nor a lookup, and `get` was answering it
at two call sites — so archiving the project you were standing on left the dashed *New file in
{project}* card on its grid, and clicking it filed a brand-new document straight into the archived
project, the one thing *Move to project* refuses. `dashboard::new_file_into` decides whether that
card is drawn and `OndinApp::nav_project` decides where `Act::NewFile` files, and **the two have to
answer alike**: a fix to one alone is a card promising a project the act will not use, or an act
filing somewhere no card offered — and `Ctrl+N` reaches the second without going near the first. Both
answer *no project* on an archived nav, i.e. unfiled, as `Ctrl+N` on *All files* already does.
⚠️ **`import_counting` is a third destination and reads `destination` too**, since an import taken on
an archived project's grid filed every copied document into it — the same refused destination reached
in bulk, and an ordinary nav rather than a corner, an archived project's row being selectable from
the sidebar's own group. Three readers, one predicate; the finding named two of them.

**The editor's breadcrumb is `Project / Document`**, and the project half navigates — clicking it
goes to the library standing on that project. A document in no project draws its name alone with no
leading separator. ⚠️ **The name shown is the *typed* one**, from the metadata block, never the file
stem: the stem is a slug now, so a title bar reading it would say `landing-v4`. The library and the
title bar share `library::scan::display_name` so they cannot disagree about one document.

**Saving.** `Ctrl+S` writes the file **and** pins a version; autosave writes silently on an interval
and never pins. Autosave is gated on `is_dirty` — an idle document must not rewrite its own bytes into
a folder a sync client is watching — and never *creates* a file, because putting something in
somebody's library on a timer is not the app's to do. There is no *Save As*: it asked where to put a
file, and *Duplicate* (which mints a new document id) is what it was used for.

⚠️ **Autosave queues; `Ctrl+S` writes (§15 D393).** `autosave_tick` keeps its four gates and its clock
and hands a `Document::clone` to the same worker the crash snapshot uses, so the frame pays a refcount
bump per picture instead of a serialise; the write, the `mark_saved` and the export all happen on the
*result*. A fourth gate, `is_saving`, is what stops two writes of one path being in flight at once —
the interval is not enough, `autosave_secs` being settable to 1. **The session goes clean from the
worker's answer, not at queue time**: `EditorSession::finish_save` refuses if the revision has moved,
because an edit made during the serialise means the file is already behind, and returns whether the
save *counted* — which is what `export_on_save` re-exports on. While a write is in flight the pill says
*Saving…* and its dot stays **amber**, a third label and deliberately not a third state: the document
still differs from its file, which is the only thing the dot answers. ⚠️ **`Ctrl+S`, the walk to the
dashboard, an open and the close-and-save arm stay synchronous, and that is a decision rather than a
remainder** — a pin is a *copy of the file*, so deferring only moves the cost, and the three
transitions each read the result on the next line.

**Every record the app keeps is written atomically (§15 D378).** `atomic::write` creates the parent
directory, writes `<path>.<pid>-<counter>.writing`, `sync_all`s it and renames it over the target, so
nothing that reads one of these files can ever see half of one: the document, each pinned version of it,
`projects.json`, the preferences and the per-machine index all go through it, and so does the crash
snapshot, which had the shape first. ⚠️ **A pin is a save** — `Ctrl+S` is documented above as both —
and it nearly escaped on the grounds that its target is a fresh name that cannot collide, which is
true and beside the point: `store::versions` lists that directory by the `ondin` extension, so a
half-copied pin is offered for restore and fails when taken.
The `sync_all` is what extends the guarantee from a process dying to the power going; ⚠️ the
directory entry is *not* synced (POSIX asks for it, Rust does not portably expose it), so a cut in
the microseconds after the rename can still leave the old name on the old data — the pre-write state,
which is the safe end. ⚠️ **The covers and the font cache deliberately do not use it**, and the rule
that decides is that *a file worth an fsync is one nothing else can reconstruct*: those two are
derived, regenerate when they fail to parse, and are written in bulk where a `sync_all` each would be
felt. ⚠️ A `.writing` left behind by a process that died is not a document — `scan` matches an
extension of exactly `ondin`, so it is not listed, not counted by a heading and cannot be opened by
accident.
⚠️ **The temp name carries this process's id and a counter, because nothing prevents a second Ondin
(§15 D548).** It used to be the target's name with `.writing` and nothing between, on the premise that
this app has no two writers racing for one path — a claim about the *process*, where the file is
addressed by an absolute path, and there is no lock file, no named mutex and no single-instance check
in the app at all. Two instances with one document open both autosave and both snapshot through here,
and the loser's handle then follows its temp *through* the winner's rename and extends it: the
destination ends up holding one payload, a hole, and then the other, **after both saves reported
success**. A name unique per write makes that a lost update instead, which is the safe direction and
the only one reachable without an instance lock. ⚠️ **What it costs is the self-clearing** — a derived
name was consumed by the next save of the same file — so the debris is **swept**: the pre-D548 name by
name from the target being written, stamped names once per directory for the life of the process, both
only when older than an hour, which is the bound that keeps another *live* writer's in-flight temp
from being taken. ⚠️ **The sweep matches the `<pid>-<counter>` stamp and not the extension**, because a
directory-wide sweep on `*.writing` alone would delete a user's own `draft.writing` out of their base
folder.
⚠️ **The other direction of that promise is the one nothing asserted until §15 D480**: a write that
fails leaves the destination holding the complete old contents and takes its temp file with it, and
`a_failed_write_leaves_the_old_file_intact` is where that is pinned. ⚠️ **"That fails" means at any of
the four steps, and until 2026-09-09 it meant the rename alone** (§15 D706): the cleanup sat in the
`rename` error arm, so a failure at `File::create`, `write_all` or `sync_all` returned through `?` and
left the temp — **and disk-full, the reason the cleanup exists, surfaces at `write_all`**. It is one
`if result.is_err()` around the whole write now. The directory sweep does not cover that case and was
never meant to: D548 bounds it to the *first* write into a directory, which is right for debris this
process inherits and cannot see debris it creates afterwards. **The destination is
never unlinked first.** `fs::rename` replaces an existing destination on Windows as well as on POSIX
(`MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING`, measured), so *"remove it first"* buys nothing — and it is worse than a
window in which the file does not exist, because `std::fs::remove_file` clears the read-only attribute
and retries, so it walks through a refusal that would otherwise have stood and reports `Ok` over the
document it destroyed.
⚠️ **And a refusal says which step failed and on which file** (§15 D715). An `io::Error` carries a
kind and a sentence and **no path**, so every failure out of here reached `save_file`'s
`format!("Save failed: {e}")` as *"Save failed: Access is denied. (os error 5)"* — naming neither the
document nor the step, on the one message the user has to act on. `atomic::at` wraps all four points
with the step as a **verb** (*create*, *write*, *flush*, *replace*, not the four function names) and
the path each is about: the temp for the first three, and **the destination for the rename**, which
is the step reachable today and the only one of the four whose path the user has heard of. `kind()`
survives the wrapping; `raw_os_error()` does not, and nothing in the workspace reads either off a
save.

**Crash recovery is a snapshot, not a journal (§15 D377).** `library::recovery` writes the whole open
document to `<root>/.recovery/<key>.ondin` — through `ondin_core::io::save`, so no second on-disk
format exists — and a launch offers back whatever a previous run left there. `OndinApp::recovery_tick`
has **three gates**, each a different mistake: `is_dirty`, the interval (`SNAPSHOT_SECS = 10`), and the
session's *revision* having moved since the last snapshot — the third is what stops an edited-then-idle
document rewriting identical bytes every ten seconds into a folder a sync client is watching.
⚠️ **There is no `path.is_none()` gate, which is where this parts company with autosave on purpose**:
a snapshot is not a document, so it can cover the never-filed canvas autosave refuses to create, which
is the one case where a crash costs everything rather than an interval. ⚠️ **The tick decides and a
worker thread writes (§15 D392).** `library::writer::Writer` is one long-lived thread with an `mpsc`
queue in and results back, started on the first job and not before, so what the frame pays is a
`Document::clone` — a refcount bump per embedded picture, `ImageSource` being an `Arc<[u8]>` (§15
D301) — and a channel send: 313 µs, where serialising 20 MB of picture on the frame took 402 ms.
⚠️ **One worker for the snapshot and the autosave both (§15 D393)**, in FIFO order, which is what keeps
a removal from being overtaken by the write it may be cancelling. It used to be what kept
`atomic::temp_for` true as well and that half of the argument is gone: the temp name is unique per
write since §15 D548, so the write layer no longer depends on how many writers this app has. Its results
are drained once at the top of the frame (`disk_results`), ahead of both ticks, because each gates on
state the other's result can change. ⚠️ **That drain reads the channel's hang-up and not only its
emptiness (§15 D549).** `try_recv` has two error variants and a loop leaving on both read a dead worker
as an idle one, so a panic inside a document write left `saving` set, closed `autosave_tick`'s
`is_saving` gate for the rest of the session, and thereby made `Writer::send`'s own failure report
unreachable too, since nothing was ever queued again — the pill on *Saving…* with nothing being
written and nothing said. `Writer::settle`'s hang-up arm had always noticed, and `settle` runs only
from `save_file`, `on_exit` and `relocate`, none of which happen on their own.
**A removal goes down the same queue as a write**, which is what stops *Discard* or a clean quit being
overtaken by a write already in flight and having the file put back. `recovery.at` is written from the
worker's answer and nowhere else, so it still means *the revision that reached the disk*. ⚠️ **Five
places wait on the queue**: `eframe::App::on_exit` — the primary, reached on every way out — both
closing arms of `close_confirmation`, and `Drop for Writer` as the **backstop**, a destructor being
the *most* skippable of the three (`std::process::exit(0)` with `run_and_return` off, and a macOS
`Cmd-Q` even with it on); plus `panels::dashboard::apply_library_settings`, since `relocate` carries
`.recovery/` to the new base folder on the UI thread; and `OndinApp::save_file`, which is the frame
about to write a path the worker may be holding. ⚠️ **The write is atomic, and
this file got there first** — a file whose entire purpose is surviving a crash cannot be written in a
way a crash can corrupt, i.e. a recovery offer that fails when accepted — which is the argument that
was then applied to every other record (§15 D378). ⚠️ ***Discard* also removes the temp file**
(`atomic::forget`), which no other caller needs: elsewhere the debris is swept by a later write into
that directory and only once it is an hour old (§15 D548), where here there may never be a next save
at all — and an hour is not acceptable for a snapshot the user threw away, so `forget` clears every
temp for the path unconditionally.
🚨 **`pending` drops a snapshot the document already contains — strictly newer, or byte-identical —
and *no I/O sentinel may decide that* (§15 D716).** Both tests had been written the unsafe way round,
with the permanent deletion of the user's only unsaved copy on the other side, on a path
`open_at_launch` runs over the whole of `.recovery/` immediately after a crash. An unreadable or
pre-epoch mtime used to arrive as `0` and compare as *older than everything*; it is an `Option` now,
so the clock settles nothing and the bytes decide. And two unreadable *files* used to compare equal
through `read(..).ok() == read(..).ok()` and read as byte-identical; the comparison requires two
`Ok`s. ⚠️ **The rule is the one `read_meta` five lines below had all along** — it answers `None` for
the same reason and deletes nothing — so what this fixed was one function holding two opposite
conclusions about an unreadable file. `Pending::written` being an `Option` is why the recovery card's
sentence **drops its *"from N hours ago"* clause** rather than inventing a time: `0` reads as *"56
years ago"* and `now` as *"just now"* about a file that may be a week old. ⚠️ **Recovering does not write the user's file**: the
snapshot loads into the session with the original's path and `mark_unsaved`, so the next move is
theirs, and the snapshot **being recovered from** is kept until they save or *Discard*. The interval
is a constant rather than a preference, because `autosave_secs = 0` means **off** and off is when a
crash costs the most.
⚠️ **The tick only runs on an editor frame**, so `close_confirmation`'s two closing
arms, `open_path`, `go_to_dashboard` and `recover` each drop the snapshot themselves — **five call
sites across four functions** — `go_to_dashboard` only
when the session is clean, or the unfiled document would lose the only copy of itself there is, and
only *after* committing the live text session (§9.3, §15 D415).
🚨 **`recover` is the second door that replaces the session's document, and it is guarded before it
drops** (§15 D681 → **D768**). It adopts the pending snapshot's key over whatever this session held,
so the outgoing session's snapshot used to be stranded in `.recovery/` and re-offered at every launch
for ever. **The one-line repair alone was written and reverted**, because the reachable route is the
**queue** — `recovery::pending` holds more than one and the card says *"N more after this one"* — where
the key being dropped names the snapshot the user recovered a press ago and has not saved, and
deleting that is worse than leaking it. **What makes the drop safe is
`OndinApp::may_replace_current_document`**, which is `open_path`'s opening four lines — save a filed
document without asking, then `confirm_discard` for an unfiled one — lifted into a predicate that both
doors ask. Past it the work has been saved or the user has been asked, which is `open_path`'s own
*"there is no third way to reach here"* now true of this door too. ⚠️ **The two are one change and
must not be separated**: a drop without the guard deletes the user's work on the second press.
⚠️ **The guard runs before `recovery_modal` pops `pending`**, so a declined discard leaves the card
exactly as it was — **a *Recover* the user backed out of is not a *Later***.
**So *Discard* is no longer the only thing that deletes.** Pinned by
`recovering_drops_the_outgoing_snapshot_now_that_the_guards_are_there` and, for the queue route the
first cannot structurally see, `a_second_recover_asks_before_it_spends_the_first` — which asserts the
*state* that forces the ask rather than the ask itself, `confirm_discard` raising a blocking `rfd`
dialog no headless probe can answer, and says so in its own doc.

⚠️ **The unsaved-close card is raised by cancelling the window close, and the cancel must be re-armed
on every request rather than only the first** (`handle_close_request`, §15 D415). The title bar is not
covered by an in-app `egui::Modal`, so a second click on ✕ — the ordinary reflex when a dialog appears
— arrives while the card is already up; a guard on that state emitted no `CancelClose`, which has
exactly one emitter in the workspace, so nothing cancelled the close and eframe took the window down
with the card still unanswered. Cancelling again is free: the flag is idempotent and the card is
already drawn.
⚠️ **The card offers three answers behind two buttons**: *Recover*, *Discard*, and `Later` for the ✕,
Escape and the backdrop, which pop the question for this launch and leave the file for the next one.
*Discard* is the only one of the three that deletes, and a free dismissal must never become one.
⚠️ **Of the three and of the app, and that is the state a ruling could change**: *Recover* leaves the
key the session was already holding on disk rather than dropping it (§15 D681), because on a queue of
two snapshots the key it would drop is the first one the user recovered.

**The screen is built out of `ui.rs`, not out of egui's defaults (§15 D367).** It was assembled in one
pass from `design/Dashboard.dc.html` and drifted, towards the end of that pass, into spelling its own
controls: the grid/list switch was two icon buttons where the design draws one recessed track, the sort
control was a bare label button, booleans were `egui::checkbox`es and every text box was a plain
`egui::TextEdit` — egui's frame, egui's margin, and the blue focus ring nothing else in this app paints.
The rule now is §9.4's: a two-way switch is a `ui::segmented` track, a labelled action is
`ui::action_button` sized by `ui::action_button_w` to its **longest** word so it cannot twitch as it
cycles, a boolean is a `ui::switch_row` (as the inspector's *Clip content* already is), and free text is
`ui::text_field`. The body header's controls — the project filter, sort, view, *Edit project* and
*Delete project* — share `HEADER_CONTROL_H = 28`, which is `settings::FIELD_H`. ⚠️ **The last of them
is the design's icon button, 32 wide and carrying no word** (§15 D379): two labelled buttons side by
side read as two ordinary actions, and one of these removes something with no trash to come back from.
Its face is `ui::button_face`'s like the rest of the cluster, with the hovered state **repainted** in
`theme::color::DANGER` — between the face and the glyph, or the wash covers what it is tinting, and
rounded to `ui::BUTTON_R` rather than to a number written at the call site. It is also the one control
here whose words survive **only in a tooltip**, which no probe can read: what a test can assert is the
glyph.

**The body header's project filter is one predicate read from two places** (§15 D369). *All projects ⌄*
— a colour dot, a name and a caret — is leftmost in that cluster and drops an `Area` listing *All
projects* and then every project, each with its swatch and a tick on the one in force. A button and an
`Area` rather than a `ComboBox`, because a `selected_text` is one `WidgetText` and cannot hold a colour
chip; the ground is `ui::button_face`'s, which is `pub` for this, since a hairline half a shade off from
the `ui::action_button` beside it reads as two different kinds of control in one row.
⚠️ **`OndinApp::filter_applies` gates the control *and* the `retain` in `OndinApp::visible_entries`** —
the design gates both on its `showFilter` and this is that, spelled once. Split, a filter set on *All
files* goes on selecting on *Recent*, where there is no control to unset it with: a list silently
missing most of itself. It is false on *Recent* (a landing page rather than a list), inside a project
(the question is already answered) and when there is no **unarchived** project to filter by — the
predicate has to agree with what the menu actually offers, and archiving is a second way to empty it
(§15 D379). ⚠️ For the same reason, archiving the project a filter *names* clears the filter: its own
dropdown no longer lists the row that would unset it. ⚠️ **The stale-id degrade runs
*above* that early return**, because the case where a filter's project stops resolving is most often the
case where the last project was deleted — which is a nav the control is not drawn on.

**An icon is the icon font's business.** The sidebar's *New file* button read `"＋  New file"` in
`FontId::proportional`, and U+FF0B is a fullwidth plus the bundled Inter has no glyph for, so the accent
button on the screen drew egui's empty box where its plus should be. It is `icon::PLUS` in
`theme::icon_font` as a separate run now, measured and placed so the pair is centred as one thing —
`ui::action_button`'s arithmetic, which cannot be borrowed here because that paints `button_face`'s
recessed ground and this is the one accent button on the screen. Nothing in this app should be spelling
an icon as a character in a prose font (§15 D369).

⚠️ **`TextEdit::frame(Frame::NONE)` is what suppresses egui's focus ring, and the same call silently
throws `TextEdit::margin` away.** egui reads that builder only through
`frame.unwrap_or_else(|| Frame::new().inner_margin(margin))`, so a caller that supplies a frame supplies
the text inset with it. `ui::text_field` gets its inset from `ui::field_row`'s plate;
`OndinApp::rename_field`, which is put into a rect the card has already reserved rather than allocated
down a column, has to put its own in the frame.

**A single click opens a document, and the outline is the keyboard's cursor (§15 D381).**
`OndinApp::pick_or_open` is that rule for the grid and the list alike — nothing
reads `double_clicked` anywhere on this screen, because the first click of a double has already opened
the document. ⚠️ **It does one other thing, and it is `context-menus.md` §0's R4 arriving on a second
screen** (§15 D558): **a click that dismisses one of the library's two floating menus is spent doing
so.** The ⋮ popup and the *All projects ⌄* dropdown are `egui::Area`s covering only their own rects
and their dismissals read `any_click()` without consuming it, so clicking another card to get rid of
a menu closed it **and opened that document** — on the canvas that rule protects a selection, here it
was a whole navigation. The gate is on the act rather than at the two dismissals, because a dismissal
cannot consume a click the card has already turned into an `Act::Open`, and it reads
`DashboardState::menu_was_up`, **latched at the top of `dashboard_ui`**: `file_menu_button` runs its
dismissal from inside the card that owns the menu, so the live flag is already `false` for every card
drawn after the anchor and the naive fix worked or not by sort order. ⚠️ **Five call sites read the
flag and two more still do not.** `pick_or_open`, `nav_row`, `project_row` — **both** its hits, the
*Unarchive* button sharing the row's rect — and the `new_file_card` call site all end
`&& !self.dash.menu_was_up`; the first version of the fix gated `pick_or_open` alone, so a dismissing
click on a sidebar nav row still navigated and one on the dashed *New file* card still *created a
document*, which is the worst of them and the only door here that is not a navigation. **The
sidebar's accent *New file* button and *Recent*'s project cards are the two left**, and the first is
that same create-a-document case — seven hand-written copies of one predicate is what §9.3's rule
costs on this screen, and nothing makes a new door join. ⚠️ **This reverses most of D372**, which made a click *select*: nothing on the screen ever
acted on a pointer-made selection, since every action a card offers is on its own ⋮ menu, so it was a
state the user could enter, could see and could do nothing with — and opening cost a second click on top
of it. `DashboardState::selected` is now written **only** by `OndinApp::dashboard_keys`. A cursored card
takes a full `color::ACCENT` border against the muted `ACCENT_700` of hover; a cursored row takes an
`ACCENT_900` wash instead, because a hairline around a 38pt row flush with its neighbours reads as the
row having *grown* where a ground reads as it being picked. ⚠️ **The body's background is
`ui.interact`ed before any card is drawn**, since egui's hit test takes the *last* widget registered at
a point: the cards each claim a piece on top of it, and what is left over is the empty space a click has
to land on to mean *nothing, thanks*. ⚠️ **The cursor is a path and can name a file that is gone** —
every action here writes to disk and re-scans — so `OndinApp::dashboard_body` clears one that matches no
*visible* entry, a cursor filtered off screen being one the user cannot dismiss either.

**The library answers its own keys (§15 D374, `shortcuts.md` §8a).** `OndinApp::dashboard_keys` runs at
the top of `dashboard_body`: arrows move the selection, `Enter` opens it, `Delete`/`Backspace` opens the
confirmation rather than deleting, and `Escape` clears it. ⚠️ **It reads `egui::Context` directly, and
cannot do otherwise** — `input::resolve` is the editor's keymap and is not called while the library is
up — so the guard `resolve` would have given is written out: the two confirmations, the ⋮ menu, the *Move
to project* sheet, *New project*, Settings, the rename field, the search overlay, the recovery card,
`egui_wants_keyboard_input` and `modifiers.is_none()`. ⚠️ **That list is `OndinApp::library_keys_are_free`
since 2026-09-08, because the screen has *two* readers of the context and only one of them had it**
(§15 D542). `search_field` read `Ctrl+K`/`Ctrl+P` with no guard at all, and the top bar is drawn
*before* the modal calls — so the chord under *New project* opened the overlay behind the backdrop and
took the caret, permanently, the card's own focus being a one-shot latch while the overlay re-asks
every frame. `egui_wants_keyboard_input` stays **outside** the predicate and is asked by each caller
separately: it is about a live caret rather than about what is on screen, and `search_field` reads its
chord before drawing its own field, so folding it in would make the overlay unopenable while anything
anywhere held focus. ⚠️ **The modifier discipline is the half that predicate does not carry, and one
of the two sites was missing it until 2026-09-09** (§15 D712): both read `command` **without Alt and
without Shift**, spelled the way `input::normal_mode` spells it, so `Ctrl+Alt+N` and `Ctrl+Shift+D`
stay unbound on this screen exactly as they are in the editor rather than becoming second doors the
library invented. `search_field`'s gate was bare `command`, so `Ctrl+Shift+K`, `Ctrl+Alt+K`,
`Ctrl+Shift+P` and `Ctrl+Alt+P` all opened the overlay — four spellings `shortcuts.md` §8's row does
not list — and **the guards §15 D710 put on `input::normal_mode` could not have reached it**, that
function not running here at all. ⚠️ The recovery card is the one modal over this
screen that this file knows nothing about — `OndinApp::ui` draws it above the view branch (§15 D377) —
and it is the only one a *launch* can put there. ⚠️ **This list had it and the editor's own gate did
not**: until 2026-09-07 that gate named Settings alone, so the recovery card owned the keyboard on the
library screen and not on the editor's, where `Ctrl+A` then `Delete` emptied the document behind it
(§15 D464). Two hand-maintained lists of one fact is what §9.3's rule costs here, and nothing makes a
new modal join either. ⚠️ **The editor's side is `OndinApp::modal_is_up` since 2026-09-15** (§15 D759),
which wanted the condition a *third* time — for a dropped file — so it is a predicate with two askers
rather than two spellings; this list is still hand-maintained and is still the copy a new modal has to
be added to by hand. ⚠️ **And it has two askers of its own since the same day** (§15 D772): the
library's drop door asks it too, rather than growing a third list. So the cost is now **two lists,
each read twice**, and the thing that has not changed is that a new modal still has to be added to
both by hand. ⚠️ **The two floating menus are the ones that do not merely
block — `Escape` shuts them**, handled above the guard list, because every card on this screen is a
`settings::card_modal` and gets Escape free through `should_close` while both menus are bare `Area`s that
took only an outside click. ⚠️ **That was written of the ⋮ alone and the *All projects ⌄* dropdown was
in neither half of the function until 2026-09-08** (§15 D578): with it open `Escape` cleared the card
cursor behind it, `Delete` opened the confirmation underneath it and an arrow stepped the cursor behind
it. The early return asks `library_menu_open()`, the predicate the pointer side already shares, so the
twins cannot drift apart again — and the enumeration above is untouched, this being the *early return*
rather than `library_keys_are_free`. The arithmetic is the free function
`arrow_target`, per §15 D269; the grid steps in **reading order** and out of range **clamps** rather than
refusing, so no press is ever dead. ⚠️ **`OndinApp::can_open` is one predicate for the keyboard and the
click**, because a document in the trash may not be opened — the editor would sit on a file the
purge deletes out from under it — and the pointer had been ignoring the rule the ⋮ menu states.
`DashboardState::scroll_to_selected` and `OndinApp::follow_selection` bring the card into view **only
when the keyboard moved it**, so a click near the viewport edge does not jerk the grid.

**The search dropdown answers the arrows, and `Enter` takes the row they are on (§15 D382).** Every
row, not only a document: a recent query refills the field and a project navigates, exactly as clicking
them does. ⚠️ **The arrows are `consume_key`'d above the `TextEdit`, not read after it** — the field
holds the caret the whole time the overlay is up, so an arrow it can still see is one that moves the
caret to the end of the query. ⚠️ **`Escape` is `consume_key`'d for a different reason** (§15 D543):
that branch *returns* before the field is drawn, so `dashboard_keys` later in the same frame saw an
overlay already shut, no caret anywhere and its own `Escape` arm — one press closed the search **and**
threw the keyboard cursor away, leaving the next `Enter` or `Delete` doing nothing. `shortcuts.md` §8a
says the overlay closes *instead*, and this was the one row the code disagreed with. ⚠️ **`DashboardState::search_row` distinguishes `None` from `Some(0)`**:
unsteered, the highlight sits on the first *document* match, which is where `Enter` has always gone, and
the recents and project groups above it change length as the query does — so the default is recomputed
rather than remembered.

**A modal marks the focused control only once a key has moved the focus (§15 D382)** — CSS's
`:focus-visible`, which egui has no equivalent of. `ui::focus_ring` paints an accent hairline
`StrokeKind::Outside` the widget `Memory::focused` names, gated on a flag that `Tab` turns on and any
pointer press turns off; `settings::card` calls it after every card body so a new modal cannot forget.
⚠️ **Every hand-rolled control here is already focusable** — `Sense::click()` is `CLICK | FOCUSABLE` in
egui, so `button_face`, `switch_row` and the swatches are all in the tab order whether or not anyone
meant them to be, which is why this needed no call-site changes. ⚠️ **That is true of the editor's
panels too and they get no ring**, `focus_ring` having exactly the two production sites above: one
`Tab` outside a modal parks the focus invisibly on a chrome control, and `Space` — the canvas's
hold-to-pan key — then presses it. **Whether the chrome is meant to be keyboard-traversable at all is
undecided**, deferred by the maintainer and recorded with its measurement at §15 **D747**; nothing
here rules either way.

**An empty list names what is missing and nothing else (§15 D382).** *All files* and a project's page
used to print the base folder path under the sentence, on the argument that an empty library usually
means the setting points elsewhere. That is true of the cause and wrong about where the answer belongs:
the path is in the Settings card, where it can also be changed.

**A project's grid ends in a dashed *New file in {project}* card, and its list in a *New file* row
(§15 D376).** The design's, and a shortcut rather than a capability: `Act::NewFile` has one meaning and
the sidebar's button already files into the project being viewed. ⚠️ **Gated on the project *resolving*,
not on the nav being `Nav::Project`** — a nav holding an id `projects.json` no longer has would otherwise
name a project and file the document nowhere — so a dangling id gets the ordinary empty state instead.
⚠️ `OndinApp::file_grid` counts **slots** rather than chunking `entries`, because the card is a cell that
has to finish a short last row. An *empty* project shows the card **in place of** `empty_state`, whose
sentence and base-folder path are about the library rather than about a project with no files.

**A sync client's conflict copy is marked (§15 D375).** ⚠️ **A conflict copy is a copy of the file, so it
carries the metadata block (§5.11a)** — same typed name, same project, same id — and two such cards are
indistinguishable by anything this screen draws. `library::scan::conflict_marker` reads the stem in two
tiers: *stated* (Dropbox, Nextcloud, a dated Syncthing marker) stands alone, while *suspected*
(`<base> (N)`, `<base> - Copy`) counts only when the document it claims to copy sits in the **same
directory**, which `Library::conflict` decides. **Every pattern is one `library::naming::slug` cannot
emit** — slug writes lowercase alphanumerics and `-`, collisions take `-1`, `-2` — so the app can never
mark its own files. ⚠️ **OneDrive's shape is a stated non-goal**: it appends the machine name, which is
what a typed name slugs to. The mark is a drawn amber `CONFLICT` pill (`theme::color::WARN`) rather than
a tooltip, because the confusion it ends happens while the eye is scanning.

**A document this build cannot open wears the same chip in red (§15 D613).** `dashboard::Mark` is
`Unreadable` or `Conflict`, `mark_chip` draws whichever it is given, and `OndinApp::mark_of` returns
**one** — most severe first — because a conflict copy of a broken document is both and the corner
they would share is one corner, and because *this will not open* is what has to be acted on before
there is any choosing between two copies. Red rather than amber is the difference the two marks are
*for*: `WARN`'s own charter is *"a file that moved, which is a thing to fix rather than a mistake in
the document"*, and the objection that kept red off the conflict mark — that it would read as *this
click removes it* — does not apply where the click is the thing being warned about.
⚠️ **Two sources, because neither is sufficient.** `scan::Entry::unread` is the scan's cheap answer
and is set only through `MetaProbe::Inconclusive`, so a document whose first 4 KB parse cleanly is
reported healthy without the rest of it being looked at — a file written by a **newer build** is
well-formed JSON that `io::load` refuses, and a synced folder is exactly where one arrives.
`Covers::unreadable` is `io::load`'s answer over the whole file, which `cover::rasterize` was
already computing for the thumbnail and throwing away; the cache is lazy and per-pass budgeted, so
a document whose cover has not been attempted yet answers *not known to be broken* and the flag is
what carries the early passes. Until 2026-09-09 `unread` had no reader outside `library/` at all
and the card was pixel-identical to a healthy one.

**A `.ondin` dropped on the library is filed in it (§15 D373).** `OndinApp::take_dropped_documents` runs
first in `dashboard_ui` **unless a card is up**, filters `raw.dropped_files` to a case-insensitive
`.ondin` extension and hands what is left to `import_paths`, which announces its own outcome.
⚠️ **The guard is `library_keys_are_free` and it arrived on 2026-09-15** (§15 D772, the library's
half of D759): `raw.dropped_files` is filled from winit before any widget runs, so the `egui::Modal`
backdrop does not stop a drop, and a document dragged here while *Move to project*, a confirmation,
*New project*, *Edit project*, Settings, a rename or the recovery card was up was filed anyway and
reported itself into a status line behind the backdrop. **It reuses this screen's keyboard list
rather than growing a second one** — a rule with one statement and two implementations is what D759
had just removed from the editor — and it is deliberately **not** `modal_is_up`, which is the
editor's: `settings_ui` sits below `dashboard_ui`'s own `return` and `confirming_close` belongs to a
document this screen is not holding, so two of that predicate's three arms are dead here.
⚠️ **No test**, the editor's equivalent being testable through `session.revision()` where this path
writes files into the library root; recorded as a gap. **Two handlers, not one dispatcher**:
an image dropped on the canvas becomes a layer at a point, a document dropped on the library becomes a
file in a folder — and `take_dropped_images` sits below the `View::Dashboard` return in any case, which
is why this screen had no drop path at all until 2026-08-28. ⚠️ **Only files carrying a `path`**, since
egui's `DroppedFile` holds either that or `bytes` and the import is path-taking all the way down. A drop
with no document in it is refused in one message rather than one per file, and a **mixed** drop names
both halves in one sentence. ⚠️ **`EditorSession`'s status is a single slot** — `info` and `fail` assign
rather than append, so a second call erases the count the first one gave instead of adding to it, which
is why `OndinApp::import_counting` does the work silently and the free
`import_summary(ok, failed, skipped, already)` composes the whole sentence before anything is said.
⚠️ **`already` is the second skip category and it arrived on 2026-09-09** (§15 D693): the count used to
be dropped on the floor, so the only arm that could mention such a file was `(0, 0)` and that arm
*asserted* the reason rather than reporting it — an import of three documents two of which were already
under the base folder said *"Imported 1 file(s)"* and nothing about the other two, and a drop of forty
pictures claimed forty files were already in the library. Both clauses are appended to **every** arm,
and the `(0, 0)` arm now states only what it knows.
`OndinApp::library_drop_hint` states that the screen is a target while files are over the window — a
`theme::color::SELECT` outline and *Drop to import*, the same statement `draw_drop_indicator` makes on
the canvas. ⚠️ **It is drawn from `dashboard_ui` on the rect `CentralPanel::show` hands back, square,
rather than from inside the body on `ui.max_rect()`** (§15 D380): the inner rect is the panel less its
20pt margin, so the outline sat inside the content instead of around it, and a rounded corner on a region
boundary leaves four gaps against the sidebar and the window.

**The library's inline rename field owes three things, and every one of them was wrong at once**
(§15 D380). It asks for the caret **once, through a latch on `rename_entry`** — asking every frame
re-takes focus in the same pass that surrendered it, so `lost_focus()` is never true and neither Enter
nor a click away can commit; it is laid out in a **one-row-tall rect** centred in the box it replaces,
because `centered_and_justified` sets a singleline galley at the top of whatever height it is given; and
it is placed through **`Ui::new_child`, never `Ui::put`**, because `put` ends in
`advance_cursor_after_rect` and the name box is *behind* the row's cursor, so the card after it is laid
out on top of this one. Its ground and hairline are `ui::field_frame`'s, `color::FIELD_BORDER` — a field
that is only on screen while focused has nothing to say with an accent ring.

**Recent keeps the order it opened them in and does not offer the sort control** (§15 D381).
`OndinApp::sort_applies` is one predicate read by the header *and* by `visible_entries`, exactly as
`filter_applies` is for the filter — the pair coming apart is what left a button cycling its own label
over a list that never moved. ⚠️ **It shows a card only for a project that has files** (§15 D380), and
**`Duplicate` stamps its copy as opened here**, since a document created without being opened is
invisible on the nav it was created from.

**A project's card on *Recent* is a mosaic of its files** (§15 D381) — up to `MOSAIC_MAX` covers, newest
first, in the design's layout: the newest takes a column at full height, the rest fill the columns after
it two at a time, and ⚠️ a column that ends up holding only one runs full height too. That rule
reproduces all four of the layouts `design/Dashboard.dc.html` writes out by hand. The arithmetic is the
free `mosaic_cells`, per §15 D269, which is what makes it assertable without a frame.

**One form-in-a-modal card, and nine modals stand on it (§15 D368, D621).** `crate::settings` owns it —
`card_modal` (ground, hairline, corner, shadow, `PAD`, backdrop), `modal_title`, `modal_footer`,
`section`, `caption` and the card's measurements — and the editor's Settings card plus the dashboard's
six (New project, Edit project, Delete project, Move to project, Delete file and the library's own
Settings) are all
drawn with it, and so are the launch's *Recover unsaved work?* (§15 D377) and the editor's *Unsaved
changes* (§15 D621). Every one of them dismisses
through `egui::Modal::should_close()` and carries `modal_title`'s ✕, so Escape and a backdrop click mean
the same thing everywhere and neither is hand-rolled per modal. ⚠️ **`modal_footer` is the one part of
the card two of the nine do not use**: *New project* and *Edit project* each spell their own
Cancel/commit pair, which is how the *"lit only when the draft differs from what is saved"* rule came
to hold on the Settings cards and on neither of them (§15 D719, D368). *Edit project* asks the rule
now — `EditProject::differs_from`, above — and folding both onto `modal_footer` is the remaining half.
⚠️ **What a dismissal *means* is still
the card's own business**: on the recovery card the ✕, Escape and the backdrop are `Later` — stop asking
this launch — and never *Discard*, since deleting a snapshot is not something a reflex may do.

⚠️ **The ninth modal was the one that kept neither the convention nor the card, and it was fixed in two
steps** (§15 D525, then D621). The editor's *Unsaved changes* card was a bare `egui::Modal` with three
buttons and no `modal_title` ✕, and it read only those three buttons and dropped the returned
`ModalResponse` on the floor, which left `Escape` over it **unhandled**: the card stayed up and the key
fell through to the editor's escape ladder underneath it. D525 mapped `should_close()` to **Cancel**,
which is the recovery card's argument arriving at the second modal it applies to — the safe arm, never
the destructive one, because a reflex key may not throw work away — and D621 then put the card itself on
`settings::card`, so it carries the ✕, the focus ring, the ground, the hairline and the backdrop with the
other eight, and *Discard* is a `FieldButton::Danger` rather than the second of two grey buttons.
⚠️ **Being outside the vocabulary is what let it be outside the ring**: `ui::focus_ring` has exactly two
production sites, its own definition and `settings::card`, so the one card in the app that decides
whether unsaved work is thrown away painted no focus ring at any point in its tab order — the gap §15
D382 put the ring into the modals to close.

---

## 10. Milestones

**Status:** M0–M5b complete. M6 (MCP + headless) is deliberately deferred until the editor is
feature-complete — an MCP surface over a half-built editor would encode the gaps into a tool schema
that then has to be versioned. `ondin-mcp` is currently a stub: op-queue message shapes and the
tool list, no handlers, no socket.

**M0 — Scaffold.** Five crates compile with module stubs, trait signatures, dependency rules.
Versions pinned (verify §2 table against latest). CI: build + clippy + fmt + forbidden-dep check.
✅ `cargo build` + `cargo test` green.

**M1 — Core model + ops + history + IO.** §5 minus Resolved. Includes the Text node model (layout
comes in M2).
✅ create/delete/insert-subtree/reparent/reorder; atomic rollback on invalid transactions; undo/redo
restore identical ids and identical state; validation rejects the §5.7 error list; save→load
round-trips; re-save is byte-identical; a v0→v1 migration stub runs.

**M2 — Resolved + queries + text layout.** World transforms, stroke-expanded bounds, parley layout
cache, R-tree, incremental update, exact hit-testing.
✅ transforms compose through nested groups; hit_test exact (not bounds-box) and topmost-first;
nodes_in_view matches brute force; property test: incremental `update` ≡ `rebuild` after arbitrary
op sequences; text bounds stable under the bundled font.

**M3 — Export: SVG + snapshot + PNG (CPU).** All three export paths, no GPU involved anywhere,
reachable from `ondin export`.
✅ SVG/JSON/PNG for fixture docs covering every NodeKind and paint type, byte-stable in CI.

**M4 — GPU renderer.** `VelloGpuRenderer` + shared `scene.rs` + culling + color verification.
✅ fixture renders on a real device; pixel test validates the color choke point; culling verified
(out-of-view nodes absent from the built scene); feature-gated GPU smoke suite with perceptual diff.

**M5a — App shell.** winit + wgpu + egui, Vello canvas composited, pan/zoom, selection,
move/resize/rotate with the preview→commit gesture model, undo/redo from UI, save/open.
✅ manipulate shapes across multiple artboards with clean 1-gesture-1-undo history; smooth pan/zoom
with many artboards (culling active).

**M5b — Tools & panels complete.** Shape creation tools, pen, text tool with in-canvas editing,
font picker backed by `FontService` (system + Google Fonts download/cache), layers panel, inspector,
color editor, copy/paste/duplicate, grouping, multi-select, snapping, unsaved-change protection.
✅ a real small design (shapes + text on several artboards) can be built start-to-finish in the app;
picking an uninstalled Google font downloads, caches, and applies it; reopening that document
offline still renders it correctly from cache.

**M6 — MCP + headless.** Socket endpoint + stdio proxy + `ondin serve`; Phase 1 tools, then Phase 2.
✅ an external agent can query/export against both a running GUI and `ondin serve`; its edits appear
live on the canvas, participate in shared undo, and survive save/load.
