## 11. Testing strategy

- `ondin-core`: exhaustive unit + property tests, zero GPU. Random op sequences preserve tree
  invariants (acyclic, parent/child consistency, id uniqueness); undo/redo exactness;
  `update ≡ rebuild`; serialization determinism (save∘load∘save = save).
- `ondin-export` + CPU render: golden files (SVG, JSON, PNG) — byte-exact, runs on any CI box,
  bundled font only. **Two of the three exist** (2026-08-22): `crates/ondin-export/tests/goldens.rs`
  compares `tests/goldens/every-kind.svg` and `every-kind.json` byte for byte against a fixture
  holding **one node of every `NodeKind`**, and regenerates both under
  `ONDIN_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 cargo test -p ondin-export --test goldens` — a diff to read before
  committing, not a rubber stamp. The fixture is that file's own, not the shared `common::fixture()`,
  which covers eight kinds and carries two dozen substring assertions; an exhaustive `match` over
  `NodeKind` breaks the compile when a variant is added. `.gitattributes` marks the directory `-text`
  so a checkout cannot fail the comparison on line endings. Every *other* export test still asserts on
  substrings and in-process measurements, which is what the goldens are there to complement: they
  catch a value that merely *changed*. ⚠️ **The complement has a shape worth naming, and one day in
  2026-09-08 showed both halves of it.** §15 D593 made SVG export linear in its def count and changed
  **not one byte**, so the goldens said the optimisation was safe and were structurally incapable of
  catching the defect. §15 D595 changed the markup of every image export and the goldens could say
  nothing at all: the fixture holds one node of every `NodeKind` and **no image**, its brushes being
  `Solid` and `Gradient` only, so the exhaustive `match` that makes a new *kind* a compile error does
  not reach a new *brush*. That change had to be checked against a browser instead (§7). **A byte
  comparison catches a value that merely changed; it cannot see a value that did not, and it cannot
  see its own fixture's blind spot.** ⚠️ **The third instance is a whole *field*, and it is the case
  this file's own header claimed to cover** (§15 D658): `effects` and `pivot` appeared in **none** of
  the JSON golden's keys, both being `skip_serializing_if`-elided and the fixture carrying neither, so
  **deleting `NodeSnapshot::effects` outright would have left both goldens byte-identical** against a
  header promising a golden *"notices … the field that quietly left the snapshot schema"*. The fixture
  holds all four effect kinds and a `Normalized` pivot now, and `EVERY_EFFECT`/`effect_name` sit beside
  `EVERY_KIND`/`kind_name` so a fifth `EffectKind` is a compile error — the same arrangement for the
  second enum in the model with the same sweep hazard. ⚠️ **`<mask>` is the standing gap**, with
  `<radialGradient>`, `<image>`, `<textPath>` and `<use>` beside it on the SVG side; one masked node
  would close most of it on both sides at once, and it is left because a mask restructures the markup
  around the run it covers and that diff wants reading on its own. **PNG is deliberately absent**: `vello_cpu`'s accuracy is not
  constant across SIMD levels — a stroked path differs between AVX2 and the scalar fallback, and it is
  the only primitive that does — so the export path pins the level, but it pins it to
  `Level::baseline()`, which is target-derived. A checked-in raster would be a golden for x86_64 that
  fails on aarch64 for reasons unrelated to the exporter, and NEON is unmeasured. That is a
  measurement away, not a line of code away (§15 D304). Five other passages in this document used to
  read as though the goldens were there before any were; they point here.
- ⚠️ **A PNG golden is per-architecture *and* per-`vello_cpu` version, which is a second axis and was
  measured on 2026-09-03** (§15 D414). Bumping the pin `=0.0.9` → `=0.2.0` moved **162 bytes over 78
  pixels of 571,200** in the golden fixture — worst channel delta 1, alpha unmoved, every one of them
  belonging to a single mitered outside stroke, confirmed by hiding that stroke and getting
  byte-identical buffers. This does not block the raster golden the way the architecture does, a
  pinned dependency being a pin where a detected CPU is not, and `goldens.rs`'s regeneration note
  carries it: whoever bumps the crate next sees a diff on every stroked shape and **must not read it
  as a regression** — regenerate, then check the residual is confined to strokes at a worst delta of
  1, because **a residual anywhere else is the finding**. It is the same primitive D304 found moving
  across SIMD levels, which makes stroke expansion — not either variable — the thing to suspect when
  a raster moves. `cpu.rs`'s `raster_settings` also now
  spells out all four rasterizer settings instead of defaulting them, because that bump moved
  `RenderMode` to another struct and `..Default::default()` went on compiling while meaning something
  different.
- GPU: feature-gated smoke tests, perceptual tolerance, not in the default CI gate.
- Color choke point: per-backend pixel verification tests, re-run on every renderer version bump.
- Round-trip gates in CI: Document → SVG and Document → snapshot cover every NodeKind. **Real since
  2026-08-22**, after two milestones of being aspirational: `the_fixture_holds_one_node_of_every_kind`
  walks the golden document and checks the set, and the exhaustive `match` beside it makes a new
  variant a compile error rather than a silent gap.
- ⚠️ **A test may not write outside the repository, and the preferences file is where that was
  breached** (§15 D370). `OndinApp::headless` swaps three things for inert ones — the wgpu device,
  `FontService`'s five background threads and the preferences file (§15 D303) — and the third was only
  half true: it pointed `Prefs::base_folder` somewhere harmless *in memory* while `Prefs::save` wrote to
  `dirs::config_dir()` unconditionally, so any probe reaching one of the app's nine `prefs.save()` call
  sites persisted its own temp folder into the real `%APPDATA%\ondin\prefs.json`. `Prefs::ephemeral` is
  now a `#[serde(skip)]` flag set by `headless` and checked on `save`'s first line — a flag on the value
  rather than a guard at each call site, because the call sites are the whole app.
  🚨 **The machine offered a fourth resource the swap list did not name — the OS clipboard — and it
  is closed** (§15 D796, D798). A headless app used to read the developer's real clipboard through
  `system_clipboard_text`, `system_clipboard_has_image` and `paste_image`, and `copy_as_png` would
  write it, so on that one path the rule above held by test discipline rather than by construction.
  `OndinApp::headless` now sets a process-wide `CLIPBOARD_OFF` flag which those readers and both
  writers check, and `copy_as_png` says so in the status line rather than failing silently. ⚠️ **A
  static rather than a constructor argument, because the OS clipboard is one per *process***, and the
  check sits at the four callers rather than inside `app::with_clipboard` — the test that proves the
  lock below holds has to keep opening a real handle, and a refusal one level down would make it
  assert nothing. **Every `arboard` handle in the process opens under one `Mutex`
  (`app::with_clipboard`)**, because two threads opening the global clipboard at once corrupt the
  heap and take the whole test binary down; that is a fix for the suite, the app having one UI
  thread. ⚠️ **The per-machine index is still the resource with no injection point** and is in
  `roadmap.md`; this one no longer is.

---

## 12. Multiplayer readiness (design now, build later)

What v1 locks in so a future sync layer is possible without re-architecting:

1. **Caller-minted, actor-scoped ids** (§5.2) — two peers can create nodes concurrently without
   collision or coordination.
2. **Ids inside operations** (§5.7) — a transaction replays deterministically on any replica.
3. **Transactions as the unit of change** — the natural sync/OT/CRDT payload.
4. **No derived state in the document** — replicas converge by replaying ops; `Resolved` is local.

Explicitly *not* designed now: conflict resolution, causality/ordering metadata, presence, network
protocol. Ops are the unit of change; everything else is future work that these four properties
keep open.

---

## 13. Command Mode (end-game vision — design now, build later)

The long-term identity of Ondin beyond Figma-parity: a **modal, keyboard-driven workflow** where an
operator navigates the node tree and edits the document at typing speed — the same programmatic
surface AI agents use over MCP, worn by a human. Not in v1 (v1 is the proof of concept); recorded
here so v1 reserves the seams instead of accidentally closing them.

### The feature set (post-v1)

- **Command line over the document.** An embedded command bar evaluating property expressions into
  transactions: `.width = parent.width - 20`, `.x += 15`, `sk.x = .x + 5`. One command = one
  transaction = one undo step (invariant 5 already covers it).
- **Leap labels** (vimium/easymotion-style). A shortcut overlays short home-row hint labels on
  nodes in view; typing a label selects that node. Labels double as **CLI handles** (`sk.width`
  addresses the node labeled `SK` without selecting it). Rendered as transient overlays via
  `RenderOverrides`; candidate set = topmost hit-testable nodes (same policy as `hit_test`), not
  every ancestor.
- **Structural navigation.** `hjkl`/arrows traverse the tree: child / parent / next / previous
  sibling. This is deliberately *structural* (children order = z-order), not spatial — leap labels
  are the spatial instrument, hjkl is the structural one.
- **`/ai` — the escape hatch to natural language.** The same command bar accepts AI delegation:
  `/ai suggest a color for the selected layer that fits the design`. This is where Ondin's two
  differentiators fuse: the request is routed to an agent that reads the document through the same
  Snapshot (including `get_selection`) and writes through the same operations any MCP client uses —
  its edits are ordinary transactions in the shared history, so `/ai` followed by `undo` just
  works. Deterministic pixel math and AI judgment share one prompt; the operator never leaves the
  keyboard. Ondin embeds no model: `/ai` targets a configured provider or a connected agent
  (mechanics deferred, below).

### Decisions already made

1. **One-shot evaluation, not constraints.** Expressions are evaluated at commit time and
   forgotten; `a.width = b.width - 5` copies a value, it does not create a live relationship.
   Persistent constraints are a separate future feature (a dependency-graph system) and stay on
   the deferred list — do not let expression syntax grow into an accidental constraint engine.
2. **World-space property projection.** The CLI speaks `x/y/width/height/rotation/opacity/fill…`
   in world space (Figma inspector semantics), projected onto local transforms + geometry ops by a
   facade in `ondin-core` — the same machinery as MCP's `place_at_world` (§8.4), which also enables
   a future MCP `eval` tool for free.
3. **Selection-relative addressing.** The selected node is the default subject (`.width = …`);
   `parent`, `prev`/`next` are relative references; leap-label handles address other nodes. Lookup
   by layer name is a disambiguated fallback, never the primary mechanism (names aren't unique).
4. **Explicit modality.** This is vim-for-design: normal (navigate) / insert (text editing) /
   command (CLI) modes with a visible mode indicator — not a pile of context-dependent shortcuts.

### Seams v1 must reserve (all cheap)

- **Mode-aware input routing from M5a**: app input handling goes through an explicit mode state
  from the first keystroke, even while v1 has only trivial modes (§9.3). Retrofitting modality onto
  a non-modal shell is the expensive path.
- **Property projection facade in core**: world-space read/write of node properties, introduced
  with MCP's `place_at_world` needs and reused verbatim by the CLI later.
- **Transient overlays in `RenderOverrides`**: already specified (§6.2) — hint labels are just
  another overlay consumer.

Expression grammar, multi-select semantics and macros/scripting are no longer undesigned: they are
worked out in **`vm.md`**, kept as a separate file because none of it is built and it will churn
while this document describes shipped code. In brief — Luau via `mlua`, chosen because the `.x += 15`
above needs compound assignment and Lua 5.4 has none; a terse bar grammar that textually desugars to
Luau, so the sugar belongs to the command bar and a script file is plain Luau; `sel` is always a
collection, and a property read across a disagreeing selection reuses core's existing
`PaintShown::Mixed` / `shared_corner_radius` answer rather than inventing a second one (`vm.md` still
names `shared_opacity` there, which §15 D607 deleted); a script is one
working copy, one commit, one undo step, widening `Document::apply`'s clone-then-swap from a
transaction to a whole script so reads see writes; and scripts live outside the `.ondin` file,
because a script the document re-runs is precisely the accidental constraint engine decision 1
forbids. MCP keeps typed read and single-edit tools and routes bulk or procedural work through the
one `eval` tool decision 2 already anticipated. The four decisions above stand unreopened; `vm.md`
builds on them and carries its own open questions.

Explicitly *not* designed now: the keybinding scheme, and `/ai` invocation mechanics (configured LLM
provider vs. delegating to an already-connected MCP client; API keys; streaming feedback in the
command bar) — which `vm.md` leaves deferred exactly as this section does.

## 14. Deferred decisions (parked, non-blocking)

**Moved to [`roadmap.md`](roadmap.md)**, under *Later · Parked decisions*, on 2026-08-19. They were
never design — they are work nobody has had to do yet — and they belong with the rest of what is
open rather than inside the description of what is built.

The one thing to keep in mind here rather than there: **none of them blocks v1**, and none of them
is allowed to become an invariant by accident. If a parked decision starts constraining the design,
it has stopped being parked and wants a section of its own above.

## 15. Deviations from the original design

**Moved to [`decisions.md`](decisions.md).** The section outgrew the document it annotates — 346
entries against the 14 sections above — so it lives in a file of its own and **keeps its number**: a
comment citing "§15 D123" is still correct and still resolves, it just resolves there. That file
opens with §15.0, an index of every entry in numeric order with its verdict.

Nothing else changed. The rule the section exists for is unaltered: where the implementation took a
different route than this document describes, either fix the code or record the deviation there with
a reason and a keep/fix verdict.
